40	## General graph walking
41	
42	The `GraphWalk` / `AsyncGraphWalk` family explores shared, cyclic information graphs independently of DAG work scheduling. Import from the package root, the `graphWalk` namespace, or `configurable-tree-traversal/traversals/graph-walk`; constructors, helpers, commands and types share CJS/ESM identity. `walkGraph({ source, ...options })` and `await walkGraphAsync({ source, ...options })` run once and return the runner, including a resumable runner when a visitor halts. These helpers accept one canonical options object. For incremental iteration, start with `new GraphWalk({ source }).createRunner()`.
43	
44	Defaults are `strategy: 'breadthFirst'`, `revisit: 'once'`, vertex-only emission, all registered visitor phases enabled, and serial callbacks. Async walking permits value-or-promise callbacks and iterable/async-iterable sources; sync sources also feed async walkers. There is no concurrency option: supplying an own `concurrency` field rejects on either family. Sync types reject async sources, predicates and visitors; runtime also rejects thenables. No walking relationship means W/C readiness or settlement.
45	
46	<!-- standalone -->
47	
48	```ts
49	import {
50	  GraphWalk,
51	  GraphWalkPhase,
52	  materializeWalkSourceFromRecords,
53	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
54	
55	const source = materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(
56	  [
57	    { id: 'note', links: ['symbol', 'symbol'] },
58	    { id: 'symbol', links: ['note'] },
59	  ],
60	  {
61	    id: (item) => item.id,
62	    outgoing: (item) =>
63	      item.links.map((to) => ({ to, data: { kind: 'references' } })),
64	    roots: ['note'],
65	  },
66	);
67	const runner = new GraphWalk({ source }).createRunner();
68	for (const event of runner.iterateEvents({
69	  emitEvents: [GraphWalkPhase.EDGE],
70	})) {
71	  console.log(
72	    event.fromVertex.data.id,
73	    event.edge.outgoingIndex,
74	    event.edge.to,
75	    event.target.kind,
76	  );
77	}
78	console.log(runner.summary().outcome); // { kind: 'exhausted' }
79	```
80	
81	### Walking sources and identity
82	
83	`GraphWalkSource<Data, Edge, ID>` declares `hydration` alongside `roots()` and `outgoing(vertex)`. A vertex is `{ vertexId: ID, data: Data }`; a lazy link is `{ target, data: Edge }`. Choose one source mode:
84	
85	- `hydration: 'resolver'` requires `resolveVertex(id)`. Its roots and link targets can mix `{ vertexId }` with `{ vertexId, resolution }`.
86	- `hydration: 'inlineOrCached'` accepts no resolver: `resolveVertex` must be absent or yield `undefined` (including a captured getter). Any defined value rejects. Its roots and link targets are `{ kind: 'inline', vertexId, resolution }` or `{ kind: 'cached', vertexId }`. A cached target must already have an admitted resolution in this runner; first-use cache misses throw `TypeError` at admission. Inline roots therefore support cached self/backedges without a resolver.
87	
88	Resolution is `{ kind: 'found', data }` or `{ kind: 'omitted' }`. The `AsyncGraphWalkSource` counterpart preserves these modes and accepts promises and async iterables from source callbacks. Inline resolutions are already resolved tagged values; await hydration inside async callbacks/enumerators. Even object IDs use an explicit target wrapper to avoid confusing ID fields with resolution metadata.
89	
90	Source calls begin only during execution, not construction, configuration, runner creation or inspection. Each runner owns independent caches and source mode/callback/receiver snapshots. `roots()` must create independent iteration; roots and each adjacency enumeration must be finite. BFS consumes roots before descent; laziness does not guarantee fairness for infinitely branching sources. Empty/multiple roots need no synthetic holder. Repeated root declarations are deduplicated in declaration order under every policy.
91	
92	For each admitted target, consult the per-ID cache, then inline resolution, then `resolveVertex`. The **first accepted result is authoritative, including omission**. Later inline results for that ID are neither revalidated nor substituted. A pulled but rejected link cannot seed resolution: inline result contents are inspected only on eligible admission with a cache miss. Unlike DAG omission, a walking omission asserts no milestone satisfaction. Start a fresh walker to refresh an ID after omission or content replacement. Requested ID is authoritative; results cannot remap it. `found` accepts `null`/`undefined` data; unknown IDs are host errors unless deliberately omitted. A cached target cannot populate its own cache entry. No `missing` result exists.
93	
94	`resolveVertex` runs at most once per ID, and zero times when inline hydration wins. `outgoing` runs at most once per expanded found ID; adjacency is pulled incrementally and cached for other route occurrences. Pause retains partial enumeration; route replay uses cached links without repeating source I/O. Topology wrappers and traversal records are copied; caller data and IDs retain identity and are never frozen. A destination and optional inline-result reference are captured when its link is pulled. This is an observation over time, not a transactional snapshot of a changing host source.
95	
96	IDs use SameValueZero, including object/symbol identity and valid `undefined`, `null`, `NaN` and zero IDs. An edge is `{ from, outgoingIndex, to, data }`; its runner-local identity is source ID plus zero-based outgoing enumeration `outgoingIndex` **before filtering**; `from` and `to` express the ordinary walking direction. DAG child edge data retains its authored `slotIndex` independently of the outgoing enumeration coordinate. Parallel endpoint pairs, even repeated input wrappers, remain distinct. Compare identity fields rather than wrapper reference. Put a durable host relationship ID in edge data if needed; enumeration indices are not stable across runs.
97	
98	`materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, selectors)` consumes reusable `GraphWalkRecordSelectors<Data, Edge, ID>`; its async counterpart consumes `AsyncGraphWalkRecordSelectors`. Both selectors return `GraphWalkCatalogLink<Edge, ID>` records with readonly `to` and `data` fields. Catalog endpoint relations differ from lazy links with target wrappers. All walking materializers, including the DAG definition adapter, return synchronous sources declared as `hydration: 'resolver'`. Async eager materialization awaits the catalog once and returns that same reusable synchronous protocol.
99	
100	Reusable walking helpers can annotate `GraphWalkTarget<Data, ID, 'resolver' | 'inlineOrCached'>` and `GraphWalkLink<Data, Edge, ID, Hydration>`; omitted hydration type arguments retain the broad union. The optional trailing policy parameter preserves existing ID argument positions.
101	
102	### Walking records and ordering
103	
104	Use `emitEvents: ['vertex', 'edge', 'path']` to select walking event kinds. Equivalent `GraphWalkPhase` enum values are also accepted for emission; `visitorPhases` uses `GraphWalkPhase.VERTEX`, `.EDGE`, and `.PATH`. Each phase invokes callbacks for its corresponding event kind:
105	
106	| Kind     | Fields                                                                                                                                 |
107	| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
108	| `vertex` | `vertex`, route `depth`, incoming `via` edge or `null` for a root                                                                      |
109	| `edge`   | `edge`, found `fromVertex`, `depth` of the target route (source depth + 1), `target: { kind: 'found', vertex } \| { kind: 'omitted' }` |
110	| `path`   | Ordered `vertices`, ordered `edges`, route `depth`                                                                                     |
111	
112	In an edge record, `fromVertex` is the found source vertex; the constructor’s `source` is the adapter. Its `depth` describes the candidate target route even when that target is omitted. `GraphWalkEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` is that union. `GraphWalkEventFor<Data, Edge, Phase, ID>` and `GraphWalkPathEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` select precise records. Endpoint data stays typed; narrow `event.fromVertex.data.kind` and, after `event.target.kind === 'found'`, `event.target.vertex.data.kind` directly. No ID registry or fabricated tree `Vertex` is required. See the [typed reference example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-references-example.ts).
113	
114	A found root observes vertex then path. A followed link resolves/reuses its target, observes edge first, then vertex and path if a found occurrence is newly admitted under the policy. An omitted target of a followed link produces edge only. An omitted root has no incoming edge and produces no observation; it increments the `uniqueOmittedVertices` count and consumes a candidate read attempt and an admitted target. Record resolver outcomes in the host if omitted root IDs are needed. Under `once`, returning/self/parallel links still observe edges without repeated vertex/path observations. Visitor chains commit before their selected record emits. Expansion follows the occurrence's observations: a pause after yielding a vertex does not eagerly fetch adjacency. BFS preserves root/level source order; DFS exhausts each root's descendants before requesting the next root and follows outgoing order. Both are iterative. Pausing between edge and vertex retains pending observations and expansion without replaying resolution, completed callbacks or delivered records.
115	
116	`emitEvents` selects delivery; `visitorPhases` selects callbacks independently. Both use canonical field-wise selector patches, including empty selections and include/exclude filters; retired aliases reject. Hiding records/disabling callbacks changes neither discovery, budgets, nor revisit policy. An explicit call-level `emitEvents: [GraphWalkPhase.EDGE]` narrows every yield to edge records, including buffered records from an earlier lease. An omitted selector returns the broad union because persisted selectors can differ from defaults. Close the previous iterator before changing lease options. An admitted chain retains its callback configuration, while delivery uses the new lease's emission selection. Suppressed/delivered observations never replay; only pending observations before their delivery boundary can be newly selected. Tree and DAG iterators use the same delivery-time selection rule.
117	
118	Walking pending-request diagnostics use `operation: 'visit'` for callbacks in every walking phase. Source and iterator operations retain their distinct names, including `rootNext`, `edgeNext` and `iteratorReturn`.
119	
120	### Revisit policies, predicates, and bounds
121	
122	| `revisit`        | Vertex/path occurrences                              | Followed edges                                                      |
123	| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
124	| `once` (default) | One per found ID; path is its first-discovery prefix | Every followed link once, including back/self/parallel links        |
125	| `simplePaths`    | Each prefix without a repeated ID                    | Excludes a link closing a repeated vertex before `shouldFollowEdge` |
126	| `walks`          | Each prefix, including repeated IDs                  | Every eligible occurrence within bounds                             |
127	
128	Paths include zero-edge roots and every admitted prefix, not only leaves. Parallel links distinguish routes with identical vertex sequences. In route modes, a root reached from another root still contributes its own root path when declared; duplicate declarations of the same root do not. Source results/adjacency remain cached even when occurrences repeat. Use `once` for collecting reachable vertices and relationships; route enumeration can grow exponentially.
129	
130	`strategy: 'breadthFirst' | 'depthFirst'` chooses scheduling independently of revisit/emission. Depth counts route edges from zero. Under DFS/`once`, the first route fixes depth: finding a later shorter route does not re-expand a vertex. Use BFS for shortest discovery depth; DFS depth limits are not radius queries.
131	
132	`shouldFollowEdge(edge, context)` runs before target lookup; false prevents lookup through that occurrence. Context has found `fromVertex`, candidate target `depth`, and `revisit`; route policies add the current source-prefix `path`. The edge already identifies the relationship; context has no required `via`. `shouldExpandVertex(vertex, context)` runs after observations and before adjacency enumeration; context has occurrence `depth`, incoming `via`, `revisit`, and route `path` where applicable. False preserves observations while pruning expansion. Under `once`, the first expansion decision stands; route modes evaluate policy per prefix. The callback types are `GraphWalkEdgePredicate` and `GraphWalkExpansionPredicate`, with `Async` counterparts. Predicates must return booleans (promises allowed only for async). Commands do not control pruning.
133	
134	Limits are nonnegative safe integers, including zero. `simplePaths`/`walks` require `maxDepth` or `maxCandidateReadAttempts` at construction; `maxAdmittedTargets` alone is insufficient. Configuration patches validate merged options atomically and reject invalid transitions without mutation. A supplied `configure({ replaceLimits: ... })` record replaces the previous limits record; include each bound you want to retain. Runners snapshot options, selector arrays, visitor records and source callbacks/receiver; limits/topology policies are fixed for that runner. Larger bounds require a fresh runner. Unknown own option keys and unknown own limit keys reject with `TypeError` at construction or `configure()`, before discovery; invalid patches leave the previous configuration intact. Tree/DAG builders and public helper/option bags use the same strict own-key rule.
135	
136	| Limit                      | Accounting and boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
137	| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
138	| `maxDepth`                 | Gate expansion at the occurrence boundary after `shouldExpandVertex`. Do not open outgoing at the boundary. A rejected expansion predicate contributes no depth cutoff. Otherwise conservatively report a cutoff even for an unqueried leaf. A returning edge under `once` alone does not trigger a cutoff. |
139	| `maxAdmittedTargets`       | One candidate for each distinct root and eligible followed link, including omissions and returning/parallel links. Edge+vertex+path still count as one. Check allowance before another pull; zero performs no source calls.                                                                                 |
140	| `maxCandidateReadAttempts` | One attempted root/link `next()`, including end-of-stream, duplicates, filtered/cycle-closing candidates and cached replay. No next pull after exhaustion; zero performs no source calls. Does not bound time inside host callbacks.                                                                        |
141	
142	Global limits drain the final admitted candidate's finite observation chain (unless paused), then finish. Depth pruning permits other branches to continue. At an exact cap, do not pull extra data merely to prove exhaustion; report exhausted only if the final allowed pull already proves all work drained. Otherwise report limited. Limits do not cancel callbacks.
143	
144	`summary()` returns detached `{ status, counts, outcome }`. Counts are `candidateReadAttempts`, `admittedTargets`, unique cached `uniqueFoundVertices`/`uniqueOmittedVertices`, `discoveredLinks` (distinct source links pulled before filtering, without counting cached route replay again), and processed `processedObservations: { vertex, edge, path }` independently of filters. Each phase counter advances at its observation acknowledgement, including suppressed records and disabled callbacks. `outcome` is `null` before terminal completion; `{ kind: 'exhausted' }`; `{ kind: 'limited', reasons }`; `{ kind: 'closed' }`; or `{ kind: 'failed', error }`. Reasons are unique and ordered `maxDepth`, `maxAdmittedTargets`, `maxCandidateReadAttempts`. Exhaustion means the configured source/policy drained, not completeness of a remote graph. Reaching `maxAdmittedTargets` reports `limited` even if the last admitted occurrence happened to be the final one: checking the next iterator result would violate the no-speculative-pull bound. To prove exhaustion, leave allowance beyond the expected admissions (distinct roots plus eligible followed links, not just distinct vertices). Always report outcome when presenting bounded provenance; see the [path example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-paths-example.ts).
145	
146	### Walking visitors, pause, close, and errors
147	
148	Use phase-keyed constructor visitors or `addVisitorFor`, `addVisitorGroupFor`, `setVisitorsFor`, `listVisitorsFor`. Flat registrations sort by priority before batching; explicit ordered groups retain group order/batching. Query wrappers are detached with shared callbacks/group metadata. Context supplies exact `phase`, zero-based `admissionIndex`, phase-local logical `phaseObservationIndex`, `visitorIndex`, and readonly descriptive `registration`. Callbacks receive walking event records, not tree vertices. Only existing `TraversalVisitorCommandName.PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` and `NOOP` commands are accepted, with absent or explicitly `undefined` `commandArguments`; non-undefined arguments reject. Settlement, mutation, subtree, deletion and chain-state commands reject. `commandCommitMode` controls `afterGroup` / `afterEachVisitor` boundaries independently of serial async execution. `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` retains callback progress and resumes without replay.
149	
150	`run()` returns `this` synchronously or `Promise<this>` asynchronously; `iterateEvents()` returns a closeable generator/async generator. One execution owner is allowed. Competing/reentrant execution rejects without poisoning the owner; async calls on the owning iterator queue in order. Closing a never-started consumer iterator performs no source I/O. Active iterator `return()`, loop `break` or consumer-body error releases ownership and pauses while retaining caches/source iterators. `requestPause()` records a request only while RUNNING; the owner drains admitted callback work to a safe boundary. `isHalted()` and `getStopReason()` expose pause; walking has no awaiting-settlement state. Source/predicate/visitor failures retain exact thrown values, including `null` and `undefined`; subsequent execution rethrows that value. FINISHED runners never restart.
151	
152	Runner `close()` is terminal resource disposal, distinct from consumer iterator `return()`. Exhaustion, limits, explicit close, and failure dispose still-open source iterators by calling `return` in reverse acquisition order. Attempt all cleanup even when one fails; exhausted iterators need no return. An existing source/predicate/visitor failure wins over cleanup errors; otherwise the first cleanup failure wins and leaves FAILED. **Closing an already failed runner rethrows/rejects its exact retained error without repeating cleanup. Overlapping async closes share the same promise.** Repeated close is idempotent for state/resource effects. Successful close reports FINISHED/closed; closing an already successfully finished runner preserves its outcome.
153	
154	Terminal close requires no active execution owner; close during an active run/iterator rejects without changing its owner. First close the public iterator or request and await pause. Async iterator return immediately requests pause during an in-flight request, drains that admitted work, resolves pending next calls as done on successful return, and retains undelivered observations. A rejecting pending request remains the exact primary traversal failure. Consumer iterator throw retains its own consumer error for that throw call. Terminal close then prevents resumption and awaits resource cleanup without synthesizing further results. Neither pause nor close cancels promises or interrupts host work. Pending host work must eventually settle for pause acknowledgement/cleanup to finish. Consumer-body errors remain consumer errors and leave traversal resumable rather than becoming retained traversal failures. Use explicit terminal close when abandoning a paused runner, and handle its retained failure when applicable.
155	
156	### Walking adapters and inspection
157	
158	`materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, { id, outgoing, roots })` eagerly copies a finite catalog. `outgoing(item)` returns `{ to, data }` links; roots are explicit IDs. The adapter maps each catalog `{ to, data }` to a lazy-source `{ target: { vertexId: to }, data }` link and resolves targets from its validated catalog. Custom lazy sources use the target wrapper and may supply an inline `resolution`; catalog links use only `to` and `data`. Any extra inline hydration fields are ignored, and target data comes from the catalog. It rejects duplicate vertex IDs, unknown roots and unknown targets, preserves order/parallel links, and shares caller IDs/data. `await materializeWalkSourceFromRecordsAsync(...)` awaits finite inputs, roots and selectors once, then returns the same reusable **synchronous** source. These eager adapters differ from lazy custom source callbacks.
159	
160	`materializeWalkSourceFromDagDefinition(definition, { relations })` requires a nonempty duplicate-free selection of `children`, `workDependencies`, `subgraphCompletionDependencies`. Roots follow entry order. Links point parent-to-child or dependent-to-prerequisite, in canonical children/work/completion order and declaration order within each. `GraphWalkDagRelation` is `{ kind: 'child', slotIndex } | { kind: 'workDependency' } | { kind: 'subgraphCompletionDependency' }`; the former name `DagWalkRelation` is not an alias. Preserve parallel child slots; anonymous omissions produce no target, known omitted IDs resolve as omissions. This adapter performs shape normalization and selected-topology membership checks, permits cycles, invokes no source I/O, and does not prepare/validate execution dependencies or assert W/C facts.
161	
162	Declared live/omitted IDs must always be unique and disjoint. Selected child slots and roots-entry slots must agree with their declared live/omitted kind; root and selected W/C IDs may name either. Unselected child endpoint consistency is ignored after shape normalization, and unselected dependencies do not impose membership constraints. Selected unresolved endpoints reject. Owned topology and **adapter-generated relationship labels** are detached, including across outgoing calls/runners; ordinary caller-supplied edge data remains shared by identity. Walking sources are explicit adapters, not a common interface retrofitted onto `TreeSource` / `DagDiscoverySource`.
163	
164	`inspect(): GraphWalkInspection` is synchronous, detached, frozen and passive on both runner families. It exposes common execution fields plus `kind: 'graph-walk'`, `sourceMode: 'graph'`, `concurrency: 1`, strategy, revisit, effective `executionOptions`, counters, frontier size, open source iterator count, pending observation phases, active visitor phase/`visitorIndex`, and pending request IDs/operations with optional runner-local `vertexToken` symbols. Tokens are not caller IDs. No callbacks, data, promises or kernel closures leak into inspection. It neither advances sources nor acquires ownership. For common cross-family wrappers and detailed-type defaults, see [inspection and execution](#inspection-and-execution).
165	
166	## Configuration patches
167	
168	Builders configure future runners; an existing runner retains its configuration snapshot. Sync and async variants use the same rules.
169	
170	| Field                                            | Omitted or `undefined` patch                                     | Defined patch                                                                                  |
171	| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
172	| Walking `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | Retain the previous predicate                                    | Callback replaces it; `null` clears it. Initial `null` also means absent.                      |
173	| Walking `replaceLimits`                          | Retain previous limits                                           | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain.                               |
174	| `visitors` and `emitEvents` / `visitorPhases`    | Retain unspecified fields                                        | Patch visitor phases and selector fields independently, under their existing validation rules. |
175	| DAG `traversableTree` / `traversableGraph`       | Inherited keys and own `undefined` keys retain the active source | An own defined same-family source replaces it; an opposite-family source rejects.              |
176	
177	Every supported configure field accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: missing and undefined fields retain prior values. This includes tree sources, concurrency, scheduling fields, each visitor phase, and each in-order field. `null` clears only explicitly nullable fields (walking predicates and `transformChildHints`). Walking constructors accept `limits`; configuration patches use `replaceLimits` to replace that record. A patch containing the former `limits` key rejects, including own `undefined`. Malformed defined fields reject atomically before registrations or configuration change; an existing runner keeps its snapshot. DAG construction requires exactly one own defined source and configure cannot change its source family. Source getters are captured once per request, without calling source callbacks.
178	
179	Public builders, helpers, mutation binders, execution options and nested option bags reject unsupported own string or symbol keys with `TypeError`, including non-enumerable keys and keys whose value is undefined. Source protocol objects can carry caller state and inherited methods; opaque data and IDs are not option bags. Path query options also reject unsupported own keys: `requirePathTo` / `requirePathsTo` accept only optional boolean `noRoot` and `noSelf` controls. Omitted or undefined controls use the default behavior, and accessors are captured once per query.
180	
181	### Options and defaults
182	
183	Choose the **surface** before building an option bag. Constructors require a source; `configure(patch)` changes future runners within that source family; existing runners keep their snapshots. Prepared definitions own topology. `run(options)` and `iterateEvents(options)` select execution/delivery rather than constructing a source. Public option bags reject unknown own keys, including symbols and present undefined fields.
184	
185	#### Tree and DAG builders
186	
187	These fields apply at construction and in source-preserving patches. Async counterparts accept value-or-promise callbacks; their `concurrency` bounds physical callback invocations, not host agents.
188	
189	| Field                          | Default / values                                  | Surface and constraints                                                                                                                                                                                  |
190	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
191	| `traversableTree`              | Required tree source                              | DFS/BFS; alternatively DAG tree-source mode. DAG fixes the source family at construction.                                                                                                                |
192	| `traversableGraph`             | Required graph source                             | DAG graph mode; exactly one defined source.                                                                                                                                                              |
193	| `transformChildHints`          | `null`; `(hints) => hints` replacement array      | DFS/BFS/DAG. Receives a copied hint array; may filter, duplicate, invent or reorder hints. Async transformers may return a promise. Null clears; undefined patches retain. Eager DAG topology is frozen. |
194	| `visitors`                     | Empty registrations for each family phase         | DFS PRE/IN/POST_ORDER, BFS LEVEL_ORDER, DAG ON_WORK_READY/ON_SUBGRAPH_READY. Each supplied phase patches independently.                                                                                  |
195	| `retainOriginalTreeStructure`  | `false`; boolean                                  | DFS/BFS only. Retains progressively discovered original topology and shallow payload identity.                                                                                                           |
196	| `retainOriginalGraphStructure` | `false`; boolean                                  | DAG only, including tree-source mode.                                                                                                                                                                    |
197	| `concurrency`                  | `Infinity`; positive integer or `Infinity`        | Async tree/DAG only; synchronous builders and walkers reject it.                                                                                                                                         |
198	| `inOrder`                      | Field-wise defaults below                         | DFS only.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
199	| `workCompletion`               | `'afterWorkReadyChain'` or `'externalSettlement'` | DAG. Empty/filtered normal chains also complete W under the default.                                                                                                                                     |
200	| `discovery`                    | `'lazy'` or `'eager'`                             | DAG. Preparation makes discovery effectively eager.                                                                                                                                                      |
201	| `syntheticRoot`                | `false`; boolean                                  | DAG. Hides an entry holder; a `MaterializedDagInput` already supplies true.                                                                                                                              |
202	| `rootWorkDependencies`         | `'honor'` or `'ignore'`                           | DAG graph source only. Ignore suppresses root W gates, never C. Explicit use rejects for tree sources.                                                                                                   |
203	| `dependsOnWorkDefault`         | `'none'` or `'discoveryParentWork'`               | DAG graph source only. Applies only when the source omits its work declaration; explicit `[]` wins.                                                                                                      |
204	| `completedWork`                | No accepted seeds; `ReadonlySet<ID>`              | Fresh graph-source DAG runs. Copies membership, satisfies W only, rejects unknown IDs when discovery closes. See [completed-work rules](#discovery-and-completed-work).                                  |
205	
206	DFS `inOrder` fields patch independently; arrays/ranges are copied:
207	
208	| Field                       | Default                                  | Accepted input                                                                                            |
209	| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
210	| `afterChildIndices`         | `{ ranges: [{ from: 0, through: -2 }] }` | `{ indices: readonly number[] }` or `{ ranges: readonly { from, through }[] }`; safe integer coordinates. |
211	| `fallbackChildIndices`      | `{ indices: [-2] }`                      | Same selection union; negative positions address children from the end.                                   |
212	| `visitSingleChildParent`    | `true`                                   | Boolean.                                                                                                  |
213	| `visitAfterOmittedChildren` | `true`                                   | Boolean.                                                                                                  |
214	
215	#### Walking construction and patches
216	
217	| Field                                    | Construction default / values                                         | Configure patch                                                                                               |
218	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
219	| `source`                                 | Required `GraphWalkSource` / `AsyncGraphWalkSource`                   | Replace the future runner's source; undefined retains.                                                        |
220	| `strategy`                               | `'breadthFirst'` or `'depthFirst'`                                    | Replace; undefined retains.                                                                                   |
221	| `revisit`                                | `'once'`, `'simplePaths'`, `'walks'`                                  | Replace, atomically validating the merged bounds.                                                             |
222	| `limits`                                 | No bounds for once; route modes require depth or candidate-read bound | **Not accepted** in a patch.                                                                                  |
223	| `replaceLimits`                          | **Not accepted** at construction                                      | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain. Undefined retains the previous record.       |
224	| `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | No predicate; callback or null                                        | Null clears; undefined retains. See [predicate contexts and bounds](#revisit-policies-predicates-and-bounds). |
225	| `visitors`                               | Empty phase-keyed vertex/edge/path registrations                      | Patch supplied phases.                                                                                        |
226	| `emitEvents`                             | `['vertex']`                                                          | Delivery selection; also available per execution call.                                                        |
227	| `visitorPhases`                          | `'all'`                                                               | Callback selection; also available per execution call.                                                        |
228	
229	Every limit is a nonnegative safe integer: `maxDepth`, `maxAdmittedTargets`, `maxCandidateReadAttempts`. Zero is valid. Only maxDepth or maxCandidateReadAttempts satisfies the route-mode construction requirement. Bounds and topology are fixed for each created runner; use a new runner for larger bounds.
230	
231	#### Preparation, prepared factories and sessions
232	
233	| Surface                                                         | Accepted fields                                                                     | Defaults / ownership                                                                                           |
234	| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
235	| `prepareDag(input)`                                             | `traversableGraph`, `syntheticRoot`, `rootWorkDependencies`, `dependsOnWorkDefault` | Graph source required; false/honor/none policies. No visitors, seeds or completion policy.                     |
236	| `prepareDagAsync(input)`                                        | Same, plus `concurrency`                                                            | Async discovery; concurrency defaults to Infinity.                                                             |
237	| `dag.createRunner(options?)`                                    | `visitors`, `completedWork`, `workCompletion`, `retainOriginalGraphStructure`       | Empty visitors/seeds, afterWorkReadyChain, false. Topology/source/transform policies belong to the definition. |
238	| `dag.createAsyncRunner(options?)`                               | Same, plus `concurrency`                                                            | Returns a promise of a prepared runner; Infinity concurrency.                                                  |
239	| `dag.createWorkSession(options?)`                               | `completedWork`                                                                     | Independent progress; external settlement is owned by the session. No visitor option.                          |
240	| `dag.createAsyncWorkSession(options?)`                          | `completedWork`, `concurrency`                                                      | Returns a promise of a session; Infinity concurrency.                                                          |
241	| `bindDagWorkSession(runner)`, `bindAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)` | A runner configured for external settlement                                         | Binding is synchronous, shares runner progress, and creates local ticket authority.                            |
242	
243	#### Per-execution selection
244	
245	`run(options?)` and `iterateEvents(options?)` accept exactly these fields on concrete tree/DAG/walking runners. Sessions expose `advance()` rather than forwarding a per-call option bag.
246	
247	| Field           | Initial default / values                                                  | Update rule                                                                                                                 |
248	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
249	| `emitEvents`    | All tree phases; both committed DAG kinds; vertex-only walking            | A supplied readonly array replaces delivery selection; `[]` suppresses delivery. Undefined retains the effective selection. |
250	| `visitorPhases` | `'all'`, `{ include: readonly Phase[] }`, `{ exclude: readonly Phase[] }` | A supplied selector replaces callback selection; empty include disables, empty exclude enables all. Undefined retains.      |
251	
252	Walking can establish these selectors at builder construction/configuration too. Tree/DAG builders use visitor registrations; their delivery/callback selectors belong to execution calls. Admitted chains retain callback snapshots; pending observations use current delivery selection. Explicit emission arrays narrow yielded records; absent/optional selectors retain the broad union.
253	
254	#### Object source and rewrite options
255	
256	`ObjectTreeSource(input, options?)` accepts the first three fields below. `rewriteObject(input, options?)` adds reconstruction/conversion and DFS configuration, **excluding** `traversableTree`; it owns the source. Bound `isComposite` and `getKeyPath` are observations, not option keys.
257	
258	| Field                             | Default                                           | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
259	| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
260	| `getRootPropertyFromInputObject`  | Root mapper with the helper's default root key    | Adapt input to the root property. Required together with child mapper for narrow discovery types.                       |
261	| `getChildrenOfProperty`           | Own enumerable object/array properties            | Return input-domain hints; both mappers are mandatory with `fromProperties`.                                            |
262	| `resolveChildHook`                | Default resolution                                | Return useDefault/found/omitted for a child; graph metadata is forbidden.                                               |
263	| `rewrite`                         | Keep / default assembly                           | Post-order callback returning typed keep/delete/rewrite-patch operations.                                               |
264	| `convertRootValue`                | No conversion; output unknown                     | Required for a specific inferred/explicit output type unless using the assertion helper. Called only for present roots. |
265	| `assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite` | `false`                                           | Provide `assembledComposite` before invoking rewrite.                                                                   |
266	| `arrayIndexPolicy`                | `'compactInTraversalOrder'`                       | Alternative `'preserveNumericKeys'`.                                                                                    |
267	| `propertyCollision`               | `'error'`                                         | Alternatives `'firstWins'`, `'lastWins'`; custom assemblers own their placement/collisions.                             |
268	| `isArray`, `isObject`             | Array.isArray(value); non-null, non-array objects | Caller classification callbacks see current unknown-valued properties.                                                  |
269	| `assembleArray`, `assembleObject` | Built-in reconstruction                           | Caller assembly callbacks return unknown.                                                                               |
270	| `assembledMap`                    | New reference-keyed assembly map                  | Structural has/get/set cache accepting unknown writes.                                                                  |
271	
272	Full callback declarations are linked from the [public symbol index](api-index.md). See [rewrite semantics](#rewrite-objects) for current/input/output domains, arrays, collisions and snapshot lifetime.
273	
274	## DAG traversal
275	
276	`DagTraversal` and `AsyncDagTraversal` traverse a discovered acyclic graph in two lifecycle orders: `ON_WORK_READY` visits eligible initial work, and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` visits structural completion after the vertex’s work, discovery, and retained children complete. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal initial visitor-chain completion (including empty or filtered chains) satisfies work dependents; `externalSettlement` requires guarded host settlement; committed completion satisfies completion dependents. `dependsOnWork: [p]` waits for p's completed initial work (W); `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: [p]` waits for p's committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` transition (C), including closed discovery and completion of every retained child. Both lists gate `ON_WORK_READY` conjunctively. Completion admission or an unfinished async completion callback does not satisfy C. Dependencies do not create structural parent/child edges; graph sources have no implicit parent W by default. Set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit parent W when `dependsOnWork` is omitted; explicit lists, including `[]`, always win. Tree sources retain structural order and parent dependencies and reject explicit `rootWorkDependencies` or `dependsOnWorkDefault` options, including configuration patches. Graph source defaults are `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`.
277	
278	<!-- standalone -->
279	
280	```ts
281	import {
282	  DagTraversal,
283	  DagVisitorPhase,
284	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal/traversals/dag-traversal';
285	import type { VertexTypes } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
286	
287	type Workflow = VertexTypes<string, string>;
288	function runTask(task: string): void {
289	  console.log(`Running ${task}`);
290	}
291	const jobs: Record<string, { children: string[]; dependsOnWork: string[] }> = {
292	  root: { children: ['compile', 'test', 'publish'], dependsOnWork: [] },
293	  compile: { children: ['publish'], dependsOnWork: ['root'] },
294	  test: { children: ['publish'], dependsOnWork: ['root'] },
295	  publish: { children: [], dependsOnWork: ['compile', 'test'] },
296	};
297	const traversal = new DagTraversal<Workflow>({
298	  traversableGraph: {
299	    resolveRoot: () => makeJob('root'),
300	    resolveChild: (id) => makeJob(id),
301	    getVertexIdFromHint: (id) => ({ vertexId: id }),
302	  },
303	});
304	traversal.addVisitorFor(DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY, (vertex) => {
305	  runTask(vertex.getData());
306	});
307	traversal.createRunner().run();
308	
309	function makeJob(id: string) {
310	  const job = jobs[id];
311	  if (job === undefined) throw new Error(`Unknown job: ${id}`);
312	  return {
313	    kind: 'found' as const,
314	    vertex: {
315	      vertexId: id,
316	      dependsOnWork: job.dependsOnWork,
317	      vertexContent: { $data: id, $childHints: job.children },
318	    },
319	  };
320	}
321	```
322	
323	A DAG constructor accepts exactly one source mode. Use `traversableGraph` for graph callback options, explicit ids and dependencies; use `traversableTree` to adapt an existing tree source while visitors receive the graph facade. The source mode is fixed at construction, although `configure()` can replace the adapter within that mode. Tree-source results reject graph identity, `dependsOnWork`, and `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`, including fields explicitly set to undefined.
324	
325	Graph sources and DAG APIs accept a trailing identity type, for example `DagDiscoverySource<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` and `DagTraversal<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>`. It flows through dependencies, prerequisite lookup, completed-work seeds, settlement, visitors, graph views/snapshots, summaries and diagnostics. Data, rewrite data, and child hints keep their existing generic positions. Constructors and helpers infer identity from typed graph sources; use an explicit union for heterogeneous identities when inference cannot combine them. `ResolvedGraphView<T, ID>`, `DagSummary<ID>`, `DagVertexProgress<ID>` and `DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>` default to `unknown` for compatibility. Visitor types append ID after their phase parameter, for example `DagVisitor<T, R, DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY, ID>`.
326	
327	Selecting an ID domain other than `unknown` requires an explicit `vertexId` on every live graph-source result, including prerequisite results. Omitted results instead supply an explicit `identity` wrapper or `null`. Default `unknown` sources retain generated-ID fallback and prerequisite-ID inheritance. Tree-source DAG mode generates reference identities and therefore accepts only the default `unknown` ID domain. TypeScript cannot express property ownership, so graph result normalization rejects an inherited `vertexId` with `TypeError` before generated-ID or prerequisite-ID fallback. Class adapters must materialize an own field, for example `{ kind: 'found', vertex: { vertexId: instance.vertexId, vertexContent: instance.vertexContent } }`; an own getter is also supported. Legitimately absent IDs retain default-`unknown` fallback, and explicit own `vertexId: undefined` retains the real undefined identity. ID values are never coerced or schema-validated. Public graph views and milestone snapshots exclude synthetic-root bookkeeping and retain `ID`. Raw runner containers and their synthetic holder identities are private.
328	
329	Graph ids use `Map`/`Set` SameValueZero equality, so `NaN`, `null`, explicit `undefined`, symbols, and object references are valid. `getVertexIdFromHint()` returns a wrapper, not a bare id: return `{ vertexId: undefined }` for the real id `undefined`, or return `undefined` when the hint has no identity. A known hint id can reuse a vertex without resolving it; if both the hint hook and resolver supply ids, they must match.
330	
331	Stalled DAG runners throw `DagTraversalStallError<ID = unknown>` (available from the root, `core`, and DAG traversal exports). Explicit type arguments type constructed errors and diagnostic annotations; an arbitrary catch value narrowed with `instanceof DagTraversalStallError` still has unknown IDs. The runner's ID type is not inferred through exceptions. Its `diagnostics` contains detached arrays while retaining original ID identity:
332	
333	- `dependencies`: `{ vertexId, unmetPrerequisiteIds }` entries for vertices waiting on prerequisites.
334	- `unknownPrerequisiteIds`: unmet IDs absent from the discovered graph; lazy discovery may still hide those vertices in the source.
335	- `dependencyCycleComponents`: stable raw-ID projections of W/C milestone cycles, including structural completion waits. A child waiting for ancestor C is invalid; ordinary child waits for parent W remain valid.
336	- `dependencyBlockedIds`: vertices with unmet prerequisites outside those cycles, including direct missing-prerequisite dependents and downstream blocked work.
337	- `structurallyIncompleteIds`: unfinished vertices without unmet prerequisites, typically ancestors waiting for children.
338	
339	The familiar `DAG traversal stalled:` message safely labels arbitrary IDs without coercing user objects. These diagnostics describe the terminal discovered graph; they do not fetch prerequisites or change scheduling.
340	
341	`runner.getResolvedGraphView()` provides read-only vertex, visit-stage, parent, child, path, and ID queries. Query arrays are shallow snapshots: changing an array cannot edit topology, while contained references and user vertex data remain live. With `retainOriginalGraphStructure: true`, DAG runners expose runner and callback `originalGraphView`, a progressively discovered `OriginalGraphView` containing first-accepted content and discovery edges. Rewrites and deletions do not alter it, but user data is still shallowly shared.
342	
343	Known omitted discovery slots retain `identity: { vertexId }` in `ChildSlot<T, ID>`; `identity: null` distinguishes anonymous omission from a known `undefined` identity. These slots remain omitted rather than structural children. Prepared definitions preserve their discovery positions when replaying the source.
344	
345	### Collection and forest sources
346	
347	All four DAG input helpers return a `MaterializedDagInput<Item, ID>` envelope with `{ traversableGraph, syntheticRoot: true }` options for DAG constructors and preparation. Pass or spread the whole envelope into DAG options; nesting it under `traversableGraph` is invalid and extracting only the source loses synthetic-root treatment. Walking materializers retain their names because they return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols. Their data is the caller's item and their hints are IDs (`VertexTypes<Item, ID>`).
348	
349	Materialized lookup does not depend on live vertex data: the source accepts any rewrite-data context R, with an input specialization retained for ordinary Item/ID inference on TypeScript 4.7/4.9. The same envelope therefore composes with an explicitly disjoint R in sync/async DAG builders and helpers without assertions or new factory arguments. Discovery results and original views remain Item, and hint replacement remains constrained to input ID hints. This built-in capability does not relax live-context checks for user sources with narrow hooks. See the [executable disjoint-rewrite example](migration-idiomatic-api.md#dag-inputs-and-actual-sources).
350	
351	| Helper                                                  | Input and selectors                                                                                                                            | Membership and identity                                                                                                                                                                              |
352	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
353	| `materializeDagInputFromRecords(items, selectors)`      | Iterable items; required `id(item)`; optional `children(item)`, `dependsOnWork(item)`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion(item)` return iterable IDs | Every item is catalogued, including disconnected entries. Any duplicate ID rejects, even the same record twice. Structural child IDs must exist in the catalog; `children` returns IDs, not records. |
354	| `materializeDagInputFromRoots(roots, selectors)`        | Iterable root items; same selectors, but `children(item)` returns iterable items                                                               | Expands iteratively. `children` returns records, not IDs. The same record can appear under multiple parents; different records with the same ID reject.                                              |
355	| `materializeDagInputFromRecordsAsync(items, selectors)` | Iterable/async-iterable items; value-or-promise selectors, with iterable/async-iterable edge results                                           | Awaits materialization, then returns an input envelope containing a synchronous discovery source.                                                                                                    |
356	| `materializeDagInputFromRootsAsync(roots, selectors)`   | Iterable/async-iterable roots; value-or-promise selectors; children yield records                                                              | Awaits materialization, then returns the same input envelope with shared-root rules.                                                                                                                 |
357	
358	Absent edge selectors mean empty lists. All four adapters reject the retired selector keys `dependencies` and `completionDependencies` with `TypeError`, even when inherited or present with `undefined`, before reading the input or invoking selectors. Use `dependsOnWork` and `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` so a stale selector cannot silently drop dependency edges. Caller task-data properties may still use any names, including `dependencies`. Structural child edges and work/completion dependency edges remain distinct. Missing prerequisite IDs are left to the existing validator. Structural discovery cycles become `discoveryCycle` issues in `prepareDag`/`prepareDagAsync`; direct runners throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError`. The synthetic holder is hidden from public vertices, events, callbacks, and parent queries.
359	
360	Materialization copies collection membership and edge arrays once. Later edits to caller arrays do not change topology; item data and opaque IDs remain shared shallow values and are never frozen. SameValueZero IDs, including `undefined`, `null`, `NaN`, symbols, and objects, retain their identity. Selector errors and async rejections propagate unchanged. See the [quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) for a complete flat catalog.
361	
362	Dependency vocabulary describes the same two milestone relations across layers:
363	
364	| Layer                                            | Wait for work (W)   | Wait for completion (C)           |
365	| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
366	| Collection selectors                             | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
367	| Sources and definitions                          | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
368	| Milestone queries                                | `milestone: 'work'` | `milestone: 'subgraphCompletion'` |
369	| Walking relation selections and definition diffs | `workDependencies`  | `subgraphCompletionDependencies`  |
370	
371	Structural `children` remain a separate relation. Walking those declarations observes links; it does not execute or satisfy milestones.
372	
373	### Reusable prepared DAGs
374	
375	`prepareDag(input)` returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`; `prepareDagAsync(input)` returns a promise of the same union:
376	
377	- `{ kind: 'valid', dag: PreparedDag<Data, ID> }` contains a reusable validated definition.
378	- `{ kind: 'invalid', issues: readonly DagDefinitionIssue<ID>[] }` represents validation failure and provides no executable definition. Source dependency failures contain one `{ kind: 'milestone', diagnostics: DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID> }` issue. There is no top-level `diagnostics` alias.
379	
380	Inputs accept `traversableGraph`, `syntheticRoot`, `rootWorkDependencies`, and `dependsOnWorkDefault`; async preparation also accepts `concurrency`. Preparation eagerly discovers and validates without visitors or execution events. Visitors, completed-work seeds, injected continuation state, and source replacements belong outside this input. Source errors retain exact identity, even when the caller throws a `DagTraversalStallError`; malformed source contracts also throw rather than becoming invalid results.
