877	### Deferred DAG progress and reconciliation
878	
879	Set `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` to inspect

880	candidates without completing their work. Enabled callbacks and their commands finish before normal deferral, including when there are no callbacks. Both DAG runners expose `summary()` and
881	`settle(id, outcome, expectedGeneration)`. Import `DagSummary`,
882	`DagVertexProgress`, `DagDeferredWork`, `DagWorkState`, `DagSettlementGeneration`, and
883	`DagSettlementOutcome` from the package root or DAG subpath.

889

891	const prerequisites: Record<string, string[]> = {
892	  a: [],
893	  b: ['a'],
894	  c: ['a'],
895	  d: ['b', 'c'],
896	};
897	// In-memory stand-in for accepted completion facts loaded from host storage.
898	const acceptedCompletedWork = new Set(['a']);
899	const traversal = new DagTraversal<Graph>({
900	  workCompletion: 'externalSettlement',
901	  completedWork: acceptedCompletedWork,
902	  discovery: 'eager',
903	  syntheticRoot: true,
904	  traversableGraph: {
905	    resolveRoot: () => ({
906	      kind: 'found' as const,
907	      vertex: {
908	        vertexContent: { $data: '', $childHints: Object.keys(prerequisites) },
909	      },
910	    }),
911	    resolveChild: (id) => ({
912	      kind: 'found' as const,
913	      vertex: {
914	        vertexId: id,
915	        dependsOnWork: prerequisites[id]!,
916	        vertexContent: { $data: id, $childHints: [] },
917	      },
918	    }),
919	  },
920	});
921	const runner = traversal.createRunner().run(); // HALTED, waiting for the host
922	const snapshot = runner.summary();
923	console.log(snapshot.readyOrDeferredIds); // ['b', 'c']
924	const work = snapshot.awaitingSettlement.find(
925	  ({ vertexId }) => vertexId === 'b',
926	)!;
927	
928	// A real host validates and durably accepts its result before settlement.
929	acceptedCompletedWork.add('b');
930	runner.settle(work.vertexId, { kind: 'workCompleted' }, work.generation);
931	runner.run();
932	console.log(runner.summary().readyOrDeferredIds); // ['c']; d still waits for c

935	Dispatch external work from `summary().awaitingSettlement`, whose `DagDeferredWork<ID>` records atomically contain readonly `{ vertexId, generation }`. Each snapshot lists exactly live deferred vertices without an accepted outcome, in discovery order, excluding queued-only, settled and deleted work. Arrays/records are detached and opaque ID objects retain identity; the snapshot does not claim host work. `readyOrDeferredIds` includes ready and deferred work, excluding visiting and completed work.
936	
937	DAG iterator events use `DagEvent<T, ID = unknown>` with required `vertexId: ID`, preserving sync/async runner identity inference. Its discriminants are `kind: 'workCompleted'` for committed W and `kind: 'subgraphCompleted'` for committed C. These events have no callback `phase` or legacy `order` field. `emitEvents` selects committed kinds, while `visitorPhases` selects `DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY` and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` callbacks. Commit timing and event ordering are unchanged. ON_WORK_READY visitor callbacks remain pre-work. Seeded W emits no synthetic work event. Deferred `workCompleted` events emit only on successful settlement, not when dispatch becomes possible. A real `ON_WORK_READY` callback can instead dispatch before its chain defers. Synthetic roots and `completedWork` seeds do not need new settlement. `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` remains automatic after W, discovery, children, and completion prerequisites are satisfied.
938	
939	The explicit `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` command ends the initial visitor chain early, discards its uncommitted buffered
940	commands, and skips remaining visitors. It emits no event or dependency success
941	and holds no physical callback permit. Already committed changes and external
942	visitor effects cannot be undone. Deferral is rejected in completion and tree callbacks. It must be the only
943	command in its result: mixed batches reject before any commands apply. The
944	retired `DEFER_READY` exported symbol is removed. Deferred vertices may expand their own hints in lazy
945	mode; use eager discovery and a complete synthetic-root catalog for a global
946	frontier, including descendants of deferred parents.
947	
948	`summary()` invokes no callbacks or resolvers and does not advance scheduling. It reports progress; `inspectMilestones()` captures dependency constraints/blockers, while `inspect()` reports execution and iterator state.
949	Its detached map, entries and arrays have readonly TypeScript types and retain
950	original ID identity without freezing caller objects. It reports discovery mode/completeness, per-vertex work
951	state and unmet prerequisites. `DagVertexProgress.vertexId` preserves caller identity;
952	`work: 'visiting'` means a visitor chain is active. `subgraphComplete` reports C,
953	and both `unmetWorkPrerequisiteIds` and `unmetSubgraphPrerequisiteIds` are required readonly arrays reporting exact unsatisfied W and C prerequisites, including empty arrays. The same ID may occur in both; `unmetPrerequisiteIds` is their deduplicated union, so subtracting C from that union cannot recover W.
954	`completedWorkIds` and `completedSubgraphIds` report committed W and C.
955	`readyOrDeferredIds` includes ready and deferred work, excluding visiting and completed
956	work. `deferredWorkIds` includes all deferred work, retaining accepted outcomes while W is uncommitted;
957	`awaitingSettlement` contains only deferred work still awaiting an outcome, as detached
958	`{ vertexId, generation }` records. Successful settlement commits W immediately;
959	accepted traversal failure removes dispatch eligibility while leaving W uncommitted.
960	`activeVisitorVertexIds` includes active visitor chains, including completion chains
961	whose W is already committed. Counts `readyOrDeferred`, `deferredWork`,
962	`activeVisitorVertices`, `workCompleted` and `subgraphCompleted` match those collections
963	and overlap rather than partition vertices. These are runner callbacks,
964	not external host attempts. `unusedCompletedWorkIds` exposes unrecognized seeds;
965	`diagnostics` describes known invalid graph structure, never deferred blockers
966	alone. Before root discovery, completeness is false. Lazy partial snapshots do
967	not promise a complete global frontier. Synthetic bookkeeping is absent.
968	
969	A generation is local to a deferred vertex in one retained runner. Accepted
970	work completion commits work and publishes its configured initial event once without
971	replaying visitors. Identical reports return `false`, including after completion;
972	unknown, deleted, wrong-generation, cross-runner and conflicting reports throw.
973	Accepted failure (`{ kind: 'traversalFailed', error }`) fails the runner; execution rethrows the
974	exact error, including `null` or `undefined`. Failure replay equality uses
975	`Object.is`. Halting is resumable and retains generation validity. Settlement
976	wakes an active async consumer; after an idle settlement, call `run()` again.
977	
978	`DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>.dependencyEdges` explains original declared constraints: direction is **waiter waits for prerequisite**. `DagMilestone<ID>` is `{ vertexId, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' }`; `DagWaitEdge<ID>` adds `waiter`, `prerequisite` and `reason`. Edges are W(v)→W(p) (`workDependency`), W(v)→C(p) (`subgraphCompletionDependency`), C(v)→W(v) (`ownWork`), and C(parent)→C(child) (`structuralChild`). Seeds do not remove original constraints, and missing prerequisite endpoints are included. Ordering follows stable discovery, then each vertex's work dependencies, completion dependencies, own work and structural children. Cycle analysis uses the same constraints; `dependencyCycleComponents` gives strongly connected component membership, not an ordered cycle witness. Summary/error wrappers and endpoint records are detached, preserving opaque ID identity without freezing IDs. Historical manually constructed `DagTraversalStallError` input may omit edges and receives `[]`; engine diagnostics populate them.

980	#### DAG summary schema
981	
982	`DagSummary<ID>` is a detached observation with readonly public types. It does not advance execution, claim host work, fetch sources or refresh itself. Opaque ID/data values remain shallow caller values. Synthetic holders, deleted vertices and known omissions are absent from the live progress map.
983	
984	| Field                    | Type                                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                   |
985	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
986	| `discovery.mode`         | `'lazy'` or `'eager'`                      | Effective discovery policy, including preparation.                                                                                        |
987	| `discovery.complete`     | `boolean`                                  | Closure of the exposed discovery domain; lazy false means a partial view.                                                                 |
988	| `counts`                 | Counts record below                        | Counts over current visible live work records.                                                                                            |
989	| `vertices`               | `ReadonlyMap<ID, DagVertexProgress<ID>>`   | Per-live-vertex W/C progress in discovery order.                                                                                          |
990	| `readyOrDeferredIds`     | `readonly ID[]`                            | Dependency-eligible ready/deferred work; excludes active work callbacks and committed W.                                                  |
991	| `deferredWorkIds`        | `readonly ID[]`                            | Deferred W, including accepted fatal outcomes while W remains uncommitted.                                                                |
992	| `awaitingSettlement`     | `readonly DagDeferredWork<ID>[]`           | Only live deferred W with no accepted outcome. Each record atomically has vertexId and generation. **Use this for lower-level dispatch.** |
993	| `activeVisitorVertexIds` | `readonly ID[]`                            | Active CTT visitor chains, including completion chains for already-completed W.                                                           |
994	| `completedWorkIds`       | `readonly ID[]`                            | Committed W, including recognized seeds.                                                                                                  |
995	| `completedSubgraphIds`   | `readonly ID[]`                            | Committed C.                                                                                                                              |
996	| `unusedCompletedWorkIds` | `readonly ID[]`                            | Seed IDs not yet recognized; closed discovery rejects unknown seeds.                                                                      |
997	| `diagnostics`            | `DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>` or null | Known invalid topology; ordinary external deferral alone is not a stall.                                                                  |
998	
999	Every count is a number. These collections overlap; do not sum the counts into a total.
1000	
1001	| Count field                    | Meaning                                                                                                          |
1002	| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1003	| `counts.discovered`            | Number of current visible live records (`vertices.size`), not all source IDs, omissions or historical deletions. |
1004	| `counts.pending`               | Records with `work: 'pending'`, blocked by unmet W/C prerequisites.                                              |
1005	| `counts.readyOrDeferred`       | `readyOrDeferredIds.length`.                                                                                     |
1006	| `counts.deferredWork`          | `deferredWorkIds.length`.                                                                                        |
1007	| `counts.activeVisitorVertices` | `activeVisitorVertexIds.length`; can overlap completedWork during C callbacks.                                   |
1008	| `counts.workCompleted`         | `completedWorkIds.length`; seeded W does not imply C.                                                            |
1009	| `counts.subgraphCompleted`     | `completedSubgraphIds.length`.                                                                                   |
1010	
1011	`DagVertexProgress<ID>` fields are required except generation:
1012	
1013	| Field                          | Type                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                    |
1014	| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1015	| `vertexId`                     | `ID`                                                              | Caller identity, including valid null/undefined/object IDs.                                                                                                                |
1016	| `work`                         | `'pending'`, `'ready'`, `'visiting'`, `'deferred'`, `'completed'` | W scheduling/commit state; visiting means an active initial work chain.                                                                                                    |
1017	| `subgraphComplete`             | `boolean`                                                         | Whether C committed.                                                                                                                                                       |
1018	| `unmetWorkPrerequisiteIds`     | `readonly ID[]`                                                   | Exact unsatisfied W prerequisites, including an empty array.                                                                                                               |
1019	| `unmetSubgraphPrerequisiteIds` | `readonly ID[]`                                                   | Exact unsatisfied C prerequisites, including an empty array.                                                                                                               |
1020	| `unmetPrerequisiteIds`         | `readonly ID[]`                                                   | Deduplicated union of the W/C arrays. Subtracting C cannot reconstruct W when the same ID occurs in both.                                                                  |
1021	| `generation?`                  | `DagSettlementGeneration` (local symbol)                          | Present when work is deferred; absent otherwise. Not a durable attempt ID. Prefer the atomic awaitingSettlement record to assembling a dispatch guard from separate reads. |

1062	### Host policy and traversal feedback
1063	
1064	`{ kind: 'workCompleted' }` means the host accepts this vertex's work as complete for traversal
1065	and allows its dependents to proceed. It does not classify the business result as
1066	positive. A rejected proposal, negative decision, or other accepted business
1067	outcome can still complete a vertex when the host's policy says its work is done.
1068	`{ kind: 'traversalFailed', error }` instead aborts traversal with a fatal error; it is not a
1069	per-vertex business failure state or a request to retry. A host retaining work
1070	for another attempt keeps it incomplete and manages that attempt itself.
1071	The progress state named `completed` records traversal work completion only.
1072	
1073	CTT treats `$data` as opaque caller data. The host can associate accepted outcomes,
1074	artifact references, or other facts with IDs or vertex data; CTT does not infer
1075	business dependencies or ranking from those facts. The host ranks a copy of
1076	`summary().readyOrDeferredIds` and applies its own capacity, claims, and admission policy.
1077	CTT keeps its default FIFO scheduling; visitor `priority` orders callbacks within
1078	a visit and does not prioritize graph work. Resolver-result `priority` metadata
1079	is unsupported, as described above.
1080	
1081	On a new reconciliation tick or restart, build a fresh runner from the host's
1082	accepted `completedWork` facts. Never persist generation symbols. Discard a
1083	runner when its graph revision changes. The host owns business outcomes,
1084	artifacts, attempts, retries, claims, capacity, and all persistence, including
1085	durable running/failure state. It overlays those facts on graph readiness before
1086	admitting work. Runners remain in-memory continuations. See the runnable
1087	[reconciliation example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-reconciliation-example.ts).

1117	The object adapter creates a synthetic root representing the whole input. Each vertex contains `{ key, value }`. Arrays use numeric index keys; objects include their own enumerable string and symbol keys. Sparse array holes are skipped. Non-enumerable and inherited properties are excluded. 1123	## Abstract trees
1124	
1125	A tree adapter supplies `resolveRoot()` and `resolveChild(hint, options)`. Return `{ kind: 'found', vertex: { vertexContent: { $data: data, $childHints: childHints } } }` for a vertex, or `{ kind: 'omitted' }` for an empty tree or skipped child. Annotate tree adapters with `TreeVertexResolution<T>` (`TreeVertexFound<T>` / `TreeVertexOmitted`), using tagged results only. Tree results forbid `identity`, `vertexId`, `dependsOnWork`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`, and `satisfiesDependencies`, including own fields set to undefined, in DFS/BFS and DAG tree-source mode. This distinction follows the source: DAG runners consuming a tree adapter also use plain tree omission. Graph omission requires `{ kind: 'omitted', identity: null, satisfiesDependencies: true }`, acknowledging that omission satisfies both W and C; false or undefined acknowledgements reject. Graph adapters retain `DagVertexResolution<T>`, `DagVertexFound<T>`, `DagVertexOmitted`, with tagged results only; only graph prerequisite lookup accepts `DagPrerequisiteResolution<T>` / `PrerequisiteMissing`. Bare `null` and `undefined` are invalid everywhere. Graph own `vertexId` presence preserves an explicitly supplied undefined ID.

1163	Child vertices are resolved lazily. Resolution options include the parent reference, depth, hint index, and the tree resolved so far. 1165	### Source callback contexts
1166	
1167	`resolveRoot()` takes no fabricated parent context. `resolvePrerequisite(id)` takes only the requested ID. The child callback consumes an input-domain hint plus a **nested** context:
1168	
1169	| Source                         | Child signature                                                                     | Top-level context fields                                      |
1170	| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
1171	| `TreeSource<T, R>`             | `resolveChild(hint: T['VertexHint'], options: TreeChildResolutionContext<T, R>)`    | `resolutionContext`, `resolvedTreeView`, `originalTreeView`   |
1172	| `DagDiscoverySource<T, R, ID>` | `resolveChild(hint: T['VertexHint'], options: DagChildResolutionContext<T, R, ID>)` | `resolutionContext`, `resolvedGraphView`, `originalGraphView` |
1173	| Async counterparts             | Same parameters; value-or-promise result                                            | Same family-specific fields.                                  |
1174	
1175	Metadata is under `options.resolutionContext`, not directly on options:
1176	
1177	| Nested field      | Type / meaning                                                                                                          |
1178	| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1179	| `depth`           | Number; child discovery depth, starting one below an ordinary root.                                                     |
1180	| `hintIndex`       | Zero-based index in the transformed hint sequence.                                                                      |
1181	| `vertexHint`      | `T['VertexHint']`; the source input hint.                                                                               |
1182	| `parentVertex`    | Restricted `VertexView<T or R>` for an ordinary parent; null for a synthetic DAG entry parent.                          |
1183	| `parentVertexRef` | Restricted `VertexHandle<T or R>` for an ordinary parent; null alongside parentVertex for a synthetic DAG entry parent. |
1184	
1185	Tree parents are non-null. The two DAG parent fields are either both visible or both null; do not assert a synthetic holder into a public handle. Resolved views are live capabilities; original views are null unless retention is enabled and otherwise grow with discovery. Resolution metadata is a stable detached readonly projection; caller data and individual hints retain shallow identity. Live fields can include rewritten R values, while input hints/results and retained original views remain in T.

1262	## Traversal orders
1263	
1264	<img src="../Sorted_binary_tree_ALL_RGB.svg.png" alt="Binary tree with depth-first visit points: red for pre-order, green for in-order, and blue for post-order" width="460" height="393" />
1265	
1266	Depth-first visit points: red for pre-order, green for in-order, and blue for post-order.
1267	Source: [Wikipedia — Tree traversal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_traversal).
1268	
1269	| Strategy      | Order         | When a vertex is visited                        |
1270	| ------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
1271	| Depth-first   | `PRE_ORDER`   | Before its children                             |
1272	| Depth-first   | `IN_ORDER`    | At configured child boundaries; once for a leaf |
1273	| Depth-first   | `POST_ORDER`  | After its children                              |
1274	| Breadth-first | `LEVEL_ORDER` | Level by level, with siblings in hint order     |
1275	
1276	Iteration emits events even when no visitor functions are registered. By default, depth-first iteration includes all three orders. `transformChildHints` receives a shallow copy of each vertex's hints; return the desired child order. Resolution `hintIndex` refers to that resulting order.
1277	
1278	In-order traversal defaults to visiting between children, and after the child of a one-child parent. Configure it with:
1279	
1280	```ts
1281	traversal.configure({
1282	  inOrder: {
1283	    afterChildIndices: { indices: [0] },
1284	    fallbackChildIndices: { indices: [-2] },
1285	    visitSingleChildParent: true,
1286	    visitAfterOmittedChildren: true,
1287	  },
1288	});
1289	```
1290	
1291	`afterChildIndices` and `fallbackChildIndices` each require one tagged `ChildIndexSelection`: `{ indices: [0, 2] }` selects two distinct child boundaries; `{ ranges: [{ from: 0, through: 2 }] }` selects every boundary from zero through two, inclusively. 1336	## Async traversal
1337	
1338	`AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal` and `AsyncBreadthFirstTreeTraversal` preserve their synchronous counterparts' configuration, events, commands, graph queries, and visitor metadata. Their adapter, hint-transformer, hint-identity, and visitor callbacks may independently return either a value or a promise. `run()` returns a promise of the runner, and `iterateEvents()` returns an async-generator-compatible iterator.
1339	
1340	<!-- standalone -->
1341	
1342	```ts
1343	import {
1344	  AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal,
1345	  DepthFirstPhase,
1346	  type VertexTypes,
1347	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
1348	
1349	type Files = VertexTypes<string, string>;
1350	async function listChildren(path: string): Promise<string[]> {
1351	  return path === 'src' ? [] : ['src'];
1352	}
1353	const traversal = new AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal<Files>({
1354	  concurrency: 4,
1355	  traversableTree: {
1356	    resolveRoot: () => ({
1357	      kind: 'found' as const,
1358	      vertex: { vertexContent: { $data: '/', $childHints: ['src'] } },
1359	    }),
1360	    resolveChild: async (path) => ({
1361	      kind: 'found' as const,
1362	      vertex: {
1363	        vertexContent: { $data: path, $childHints: await listChildren(path) },
1364	      },
1365	    }),
1366	  },
1367	});
1368	
1369	for await (const event of traversal.createRunner().iterateEvents({
1370	  emitEvents: [DepthFirstPhase.PRE_ORDER],
1371	})) {
1372	  console.log(event.vertex.getData());
1373	}
1374	```
1375	
1376	Set `concurrency` to a positive integer to bound invoked callbacks; the default is `Infinity`. Async tree runners may prefetch child callbacks after the parent event boundary. Under timing-independent adapters and visitors, they provide qualified parity with synchronous tree runners: event values and final topology match, but callback timing and the resolved prefix visible to a callback can differ. Async DAG traversal guarantees dependency ordering and committed lifecycle ordering, not a complete event-sequence match with synchronous DAG traversal.
1377	
1378	## Visitors and commands
1379

1380	Visitors receive `(vertex, options)` and may return `{ commands: [...] }`. Commands apply to the resolved tree; they do not mutate the original input object.
1381	
1382	| Command                     | Effect                                                                                  |
1383	| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1384	| `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION`     | Defer DAG initial work; must be the sole command in its result                          |
1385	| `NOOP`                      | No change                                                                               |
1386	| `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL`           | Pause after the current visitor's command batch                                         |
1387	| `DELETE_TREE_SUBTREE`       | Tree runners: remove this vertex and its resolved subtree, skipping pending descendants |
1388	| `DELETE_DAG_VERTEX_CASCADE` | DAG runners: remove this vertex, W/C dependents and orphaned descendants                |
1389	| `REWRITE_VERTEX_DATA`       | Replace data using `{ newData }`, including `null` or `undefined`                       |
1390	| `SKIP_REMAINING_CHILDREN`   | Skip pending local child expansion; retain already resolved descendants                 |
1391	| `REWRITE_CHILD_HINTS`       | Replace pending child hints using `{ newHints }` before descent                         |
1392	| `SET_VISITOR_CHAIN_STATE`   | Set phase-chain-local callback state with `{ state }`                                   |
1393	
1394	A command payload is nested under `commandArguments`, beside `commandName`. Parameterless commands omit arguments (explicit undefined is also accepted); payload commands require their declared argument record.

Deleted vertices have no further visitor calls or yielded events.

Adjacent `afterGroup` visitors buffer commands until the next `afterEachVisitor` or phase end. Changing batching alone never changes callback order. This intentionally corrects the historical group-first order.
1448

Callback closures remain shared references; frozen group metadata/identity is retained for list/set round trips. Apply changes through `setVisitorsFor`, `addVisitorFor`/`addVisitorGroupFor`, or `configure`. Raw registration fields are private. To regroup records, project `{ visitor, priority }` and set the new group policy. Caller definitions have no `addedIndex` policy. 1457	## Pause and resume
1458	
1459	<!-- standalone -->
1460	
1461	```ts
1462	import {
1463	  DepthFirstTreeTraversal,
1464	  DepthFirstPhase,
1465	  ObjectTreeSource,
1466	  TraversalVisitorCommandName,
1467	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
1468	
1469	const traversal = new DepthFirstTreeTraversal({
1470	  traversableTree: new ObjectTreeSource({ a: 1, b: 2 }),
1471	});
1472	traversal.addVisitorFor(DepthFirstPhase.PRE_ORDER, (vertex) => {
1473	  if (vertex.getData().key === 'a') {
1474	    return {
1475	      commands: [{ commandName: TraversalVisitorCommandName.PAUSE_TRAVERSAL }],
1476	    };
1477	  }
1478	  return undefined;
1479	});
1480	const runner = traversal.createRunner().run(); // HALTED
1481	runner.run(); // finishes the remaining visitors and traversal
1482	```
1483	
1484	All eight runner interfaces expose `requestPause(): boolean`. It returns true only for a new request while RUNNING; INITIAL, already-requested, HALTED, FINISHED and FAILED return false without driving execution or rethrowing a retained error. The method records a request; the active owner acknowledges it at a safe boundary after admitted chains drain. Callbacks are not canceled and future source admissions stop. A suspended iterator may require another `next()` or `return()` to reach that boundary. Resume with run/iteration without replaying committed work. During async preparation, admitted source callbacks can delay acknowledgement too.
1485	
1486	Breaking a `for...of` iteration also pauses the runner. Resume the same runner with `run()` or a new `iterateEvents()` call. Completed visitors and yielded events are not repeated. A pause can occur even when its event is excluded from iteration. After its visitor chain completes on resumption, the observation is delivered only if the effective selector includes it.
1487	
1488	`iterateEvents()` and `run()` accept independent selectors: `emitEvents` selects event kinds (tree phases, DAG `'workCompleted' | 'subgraphCompleted'`, or walking `'vertex' | 'edge' | 'path'`); `visitorPhases: 'all' | { include: readonly Order[] } | { exclude: readonly Order[] }` selects callbacks. Empty include disables callbacks, empty exclude runs all, and empty emission suppresses events without disabling callbacks. Each supplied field patches the previous effective value; omitted fields, `{}`, and no argument retain it. Caller arrays are copied on activation. An admitted chain keeps its callback selection through its boundary. Event selection uses the effective selector at delivery, including observations buffered before a pause.
1489	
1490	Retired `iterateOver`, `enableVisitorFunctionsFor`, and `disableVisitorFunctionsFor` keys reject, including present undefined values. Malformed selectors, invalid family kinds/phases, removed `emitPhases`, and unknown execution keys reject before configuration changes. Inspection exposes canonical selectors under `executionOptions`. Only one iterator may own a runner; close it before resuming elsewhere.
1491	
1492	`getStopReason(): TraversalStopReason | null` and inspection `stopReason` distinguish `prepared`, `paused`, `awaitingSettlement`, `finished`, and `failed`. Successful DAG preview reports prepared. INITIAL/RUNNING return null. `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL`/iterator return reports paused only after admitted chains drain; deferred quiescence reports awaitingSettlement. Successful settlement while halted preserves the preceding stop reason until resume clears it. Failed settlement reports failed with the exact error. The same contract applies to async execution/session surfaces.
1493	
1494	Statuses are `INITIAL`, `RUNNING`, `HALTED`, `FINISHED`, and `FAILED`. Running a finished runner has no effect; use `createRunner()` for a fresh traversal. Errors from adapters, visitors, sorting, or traversal execution propagate and leave the runner `FAILED`. Later attempts to run or iterate it rethrow the original thrown value. Its partially resolved tree remains available for inspection; retry with a fresh runner after correcting the cause.
1495	
1496	An error in the consumer's `for...of` body closes that iterator and leaves the runner `HALTED`, so it can be resumed. Runners are in-memory continuations, not serializable checkpoints. Raw `traversalRunnerInternalObjects` injection is removed and rejects at runtime. Create runners through builders or prepared DAGs; there is no public state-restoration constructor.
1497	
1498	Async iteration uses the same one-owner rule. Calling `return()` on an active async iterator requests a halt immediately, including while `next()` is waiting on an adapter, then drains only already-started visitor-chain work. Unresolved `next()` calls finish as done and buffered events remain available on resume. User callbacks are not cancelled, so a pending visitor can delay close indefinitely. A loop-body error follows JavaScript iterator-close semantics and remains the reported error; the runner is resumable unless traversal itself failed.
1499	
1500	## Inspection and execution
1501	
1502	`getStopReason()` reports the stop cause; every runner also has synchronous `inspect()`. For tree/DAG runners, inspection returns a detached, frozen snapshot with status, traversal kind, source mode, execution mode, effective concurrency, ready visits, frames, visitor chains, pending callback identities, event boundaries, physical in-flight callback count, and buffered event count. Inspection never calls user code, consumes an event, or advances traversal, and snapshots contain reference ids rather than callback functions, promises, or vertex data. Pending boundary and buffered event counts include recorded observations regardless of the current delivery selection; they describe separate kernel/session queues and should not be summed as unique observations.
1503	
1504	`TreeDagExecutionInspection<Phase>` retains the concrete runner's callback phase type. `readyVisits[].phase` and `chains[].phase` name callback phases; chain `state` is `running | paused | done | invalid`, and `visitorIndex` identifies its current position. Each chain retains its admitted `executionOptions` and exposes `commandCommitMode`. The chain snapshot’s `visitorPhases` governs that chain; its `emitEvents` is historical configuration only. Top-level `executionOptions.emitEvents` governs current delivery, including events committed by older chains. Pending requests use `operation: resolveRoot | resolveChild | resolvePrerequisite | transformChildHints | getVertexIdFromHint | visit`. Frame `stage`, detached owner tokens, `waitingFor`, and request validity describe execution mechanics; owner tokens are runner-local identities, not vertex IDs. Walking likewise uses callback `phase`, `visitorIndex`, and pending request `operation` with its own operation vocabulary.
1505	
1506	Resolved graph vertices expose `visitStage: ResolvedVisitStage`; query it with `getVisitStageOf(ref)`. Stages are `DISCOVERED`, `INITIAL_VISIT_ELIGIBLE`, `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED`, `INITIAL_VISIT_COMMITTED`, `COMPLETION_VISIT_ELIGIBLE`, and `COMPLETE`. These preserve each family's scheduling boundaries: tree initial callbacks can still be `INITIAL_VISIT_ELIGIBLE` while DAG initial callbacks are `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED`. A stage does not establish callback activity. Deferred DAG work can remain `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED` after all callbacks drain; completion eligibility precedes completion callbacks and committed C. Use inspection's in-flight count/chains for callback activity and DAG `summary()` / milestone queries for W/C facts, independently of visit stages. Original graph views retain structural queries without visit stages; runner `getStatus()` remains the separate execution lifecycle.
1507	
1508	```ts
1509	const asyncRunner = traversal.createRunner();
1510	const iterator = asyncRunner.iterateEvents();
1511	const next = iterator.next();
1512	const snapshot = asyncRunner.inspect();
1513	console.log(snapshot.pendingRequests, snapshot.inFlightCallbackCount);
1514	await next;
1515	await iterator.return();
1516	```
1517	
1518	Every family filters observations at delivery. A resumed iterator with only POST_ORDER selected suppresses a buffered PRE_ORDER event; an event committed while emission was disabled can still be selected if it has not yet reached delivery. Deferred DAG settlement records its committed work observation independently of the selector used to admit the work. Filtering never repeats callbacks, resolutions or committed W/C transitions. Once an observation has been delivered or suppressed at delivery, it is consumed and cannot be recovered by changing the selector.
1519	
1520	Explicit required `emitEvents` arrays narrow iterator results to their selected kinds/phases on concrete runners and execution capabilities; an empty array yields `never`. No argument, an undefined selector or options with an optional selector retain the broad event type because the persisted policy is unknown. Heterogeneous unions can also retain broad inference; preserve the family capability when wrapping a runner. `SelectedTraversalEvent<Event, Kind>` describes the selected public record while retaining its data, ID and observation facets. There is no timing-policy option.
1521	
1522	Root flags describe family-specific boundaries. Tree `isTreeRoot` and DAG `isGraphRoot` identify the resolved container root. There is no separate traversal-start predicate or subtree-start option. Synthetic graph holders are bookkeeping and hidden from public events, views, and source-context parent fields. Walking uses `via: null` for an entry occurrence; under route policies, the same ID reached through a link has a non-null `via`. These meanings do not imply a shared root flag.
1523	
1524	The six tree/DAG runners use the same explicit transition-state model. Synchronous runners execute its callback requests inline; asynchronous runners delegate iteration and `run()` to one shared internal async session with serialized state commits, finite callback limiting when configured, and one iterator lease. Calling `run()` while an iterator owns that session rejects rather than starting a second execution.
1525	
1526	For reusable wrappers, use `TraversalExecutionState` (`getStatus`, `getStopReason`, `isHalted`, `inspect`, `requestPause`), `SyncTraversalExecution<Phase, Event>`, or `AsyncTraversalExecution<Phase, Event>`. Run returns this / Promise of this; iterators are closeable `Generator<Event, void, unknown>` / `AsyncGenerator<Event, void, unknown>`. Preserve the family's phase enum: a DFS abstraction rejects DAG phases and cannot widen to accept them. The emitted-kind default is `EmissionKind<Phase>`: DAG emission accepts committed `workCompleted`/`subgraphCompleted` names, and visitor selection accepts `ON_WORK_READY`/`ON_SUBGRAPH_READY`.
1527	
1528	All three capabilities default inspection to `ExecutionInspection`, which accepts tree, DAG and walking runners. Its common fields are status, stop reason, pause request, kind, execution mode, in-flight callback count and buffered event count. Concrete tree/DAG runners explicitly expose `TreeDagExecutionInspection<Phase>`; walkers expose `GraphWalkInspection`. Generalizing inspection never widens supported phases or promises another family's detailed fields. Concrete builders implement their public contracts directly; sources implement `TreeSource` structurally. `TreeTraversalEvent` remains the tree event record.

1586	## Views, handles, identity and paths
1587	
1588	<a id="safe-tree-queries"></a>
1589	
1590	Use `runner.getResolvedTreeView()` or a standalone store’s `asReadOnly()` for tree queries. `ResolvedTreeView<T>` has `getRoot`, `has`, `getChildrenOf`, `getParentOf`, `requirePathTo`, and `getResolutionContextOf`. `ResolvedGraphView<T, ID>` is available through `getResolvedGraphView()`. Both are stable live query capabilities with frozen detached collections and restricted vertex handles. DAG runners return the tree facade in tree-source mode and null in graph-source mode. Ordinary runners have no `getResolvedTreeStore()` method; edit through visitor commands or construct a standalone `ResolvedTreeStore` for advanced editing.
1591	
1592	`VertexHandle<T>` exposes `getRefId()` and `getValue()` without editing authority. `getValue()` returns a frozen `VertexView<T>` with readonly `$data` and `$childHints` fields, query methods, and detached frozen hint arrays. The handle is canonical across callbacks, source contexts, events, and query views; its value remains live. An event’s `vertex` wraps the value captured for that event, so later commands can change its live `vertexRef` without changing the recorded vertex. `clone()` creates a separate editable `Vertex` and hint collection. Opaque caller data, IDs, and individual hint payloads retain identity and are not frozen. `MutableRef<T>` and mutable `Vertex<T>` remain standalone advanced editing capabilities. A `TreeVertexRecord` stores `metadata` and structural `children`, separate from the Vertex payload/hint fields `$data` and `$childHints`. Graph wrappers use `ResolvedGraphVertex`, `ResolvedVisitStage`, and `StructuralChildEdge`.
1593	
1594	Tree callback and source contexts expose `resolvedTreeView`; graph contexts expose `resolvedGraphView`. Neither exposes a live mutable store. Source resolution metadata is a stable frozen projection. For a synthetic DAG entry slot, `parentVertex` and `parentVertexRef` are both null; ordinary graph parents and tree parents are non-null restricted facets. Entry-slot `depth`, `hintIndex`, and `vertexHint` retain their discovery meanings. Original tree and graph views remain in the input type domain.
1595	
1596	`MutableRef.getRefId()` is the generated reference UUID. `ResolvedGraphView.requireVertexId(ref)` returns the host's arbitrary vertex ID and `getVertexRefById(id)` returns its reference. Live and original graph views use the same names. Retired `getId`, `getIdOf`, and `getVertexById` aliases are removed. Do not substitute the reference UUID for a host ID or stringify object/symbol/undefined IDs.
1597	
1598	`ResolvedTreeStore.requirePathTo(ref, { noRoot?, noSelf? })` returns the resolved ancestry in root-to-vertex order and throws if the reference is absent from that tree. Original-tree paths use the retained view’s own references. Deleting a resolved vertex removes its resolved descendants and detaches it from its parent; deleting the root clears the root pointer.

1600	<a id="explicit-input-ownership-and-query-names"></a>
1601	
1602	`VertexContentInput.$childHints` and `REWRITE_CHILD_HINTS.newHints` accept readonly collections. A standalone `Vertex` copies hint membership at construction and for every `clone()` path; individual hint elements and `$data` retain caller identity. `getChildHints()` returns the owned editable standalone collection, while observed `VertexView` collections remain frozen and detached.

1604	`isChildExpansionSkipped(ref)` answers whether DFS explicitly skipped expansion; it is independent of hint emptiness and structural leaf status. `requireVertexId`, `requirePathsTo` and tree `requirePathTo` throw for absent handles; nullable sibling queries retain their documented absence results. Null and undefined remain valid vertex IDs, never missing-identity sentinels.

1614	    resolveRoot: () => ({
1615	      kind: 'found',
1616	      vertex: {

1618	        vertexContent: { $data: 'root', $childHints: ['leaf'] },
1619	      },
1620	    }),
1621	    resolveChild: (id) => ({
1622	      kind: 'found',
1623	      vertex: {
1624	        vertexId: id,
1625	        vertexContent: { $data: id, $childHints: [] },
1626	      },
1627	    }),
1628	  },
1629	})
1630	  .createRunner()
1631	  .prepare();
1632	const view = runner.getResolvedGraphView();
1633	const leaf = view.getVertexRefById('leaf');
1634	if (leaf === null || !view.has(leaf)) throw new Error('Expected a live leaf');
1635	const paths = view.requirePathsTo(leaf);
1636	const ids = paths[0]!.map((ref) => view.requireVertexId(ref));
1637	if (paths.length !== 1 || ids.join(',') !== 'root,leaf') {

1642	For optional lookup, `getVertexRefById` returns null when no live ID is present. Graph `get`, `getParentsOf`, `getChildrenOf` and `getVisitStageOf` return null for absent handles; `has` returns a boolean. `requireVertexId` and required path queries throw instead. Known omitted IDs have milestone facts without a live handle. Graph paths can contain multiple structural routes; tree ancestry has one path. View collections are detached and readonly; use visitor commands to change an active runner.

1644	## Rewrite objects
1645	
1646	`rewriteObject` is callable at the package root and the rewrite subpath. The `objectRewrite` namespace contains the same callable and `rewriteObjectAs`:
1647	
1648	<!-- standalone -->
1649	
1650	```ts
1651	import { rewriteObject } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
1652	
1653	const input = { keep: 1, remove: 2, nested: [3] };
1654	const result = rewriteObject(input, {
1655	  rewrite: ({ key, value }) => {
1656	    if (key === 'remove') return { kind: 'delete' };
1657	    if (typeof value === 'number')
1658	      return { kind: 'rewrite', patch: { value: value * 10 } };
1659	    return undefined;
1660	  },
1661	});
1662	console.log(result.getOutputResult()); // { kind: 'present', value: { keep: 10, nested: [30] } }; input is unchanged
1663	```
1664	
1665	| Root operation   | getOutputResult()                       |
1666	| ---------------- | --------------------------------------- |
1667	| Retain null      | `{ kind: 'present', value: null }`      |
1668	| Retain undefined | `{ kind: 'present', value: undefined }` |
1669	| Delete the root  | `{ kind: 'absent' }`                    |
1670	
1671	<!-- standalone -->
1672	
1673	```ts
1674	import { rewriteObject } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
1675	
1676	for (const input of [null, undefined]) {
1677	  const output = rewriteObject(input).getOutputResult();
1678	  if (output.kind !== 'present' || output.value !== input) {
1679	    throw new Error('Expected a retained present root');
1680	  }
1681	}
1682	const removed = rewriteObject(
1683	  { keep: 1 },
1684	  {
1685	    rewrite: () => ({ kind: 'delete' }),
1686	  },
1687	).getOutputResult();
1688	if (removed.kind !== 'absent') throw new Error('Expected root absence');
1689	```
1690	
1691	Rewrites run in post-order. Return `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { key, value } }` to rename or replace a property, `{ kind: 'delete' }` to remove it, or `undefined` / `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Composite parents are reconstructed from their processed children. Arrays default to `arrayIndexPolicy: 'compactInTraversalOrder'`. Choose `'preserveNumericKeys'` to retain numeric positions and holes; output length is the larger of the original array length and highest assigned index plus one, preserving trailing holes and holes left by deletion. Non-arrays classified as arrays derive length from assigned indices. Numeric keys must be integers from 0 through 2^32-2. Named array properties remain supported. Built-in reconstruction defaults to `propertyCollision: 'error'`; `'firstWins'` and `'lastWins'` resolve duplicate normalized JavaScript property keys explicitly. Number/string equivalents collide, while distinct symbols retain identity. Custom `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` callbacks own placement and collision behavior for their respective composites. Null and undefined values remain present; deleting the root produces `{ kind: 'absent' }` from `getOutputResult()`.
1692	
1693	Set `assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite: true` to receive `assembledComposite` alongside the original property. Configurable classification options are `isArray` and `isObject`. Bound callback/binder observations include `isComposite`, `isArray`, `isObject`, and callback `getKeyPath({ noRoot: true })`; `isComposite` and `getKeyPath` are not configuration options. Custom `isArray`/`isObject` and `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` functions support specialized reconstruction. Default reconstruction is for plain objects and arrays; it does not preserve prototypes, descriptors, collection types, or identity shared between branches.
1694	
1695	`rewriteObject` retains its six generic positions, but default `Out` is now `unknown`: reconstruction and arbitrary rewrites cannot promise input shape/prototype preservation. A `convertRootValue(value: unknown, context: { readonly complete: boolean })` converter can infer its return type. A specific `Out` requires this converter, including when supplied through explicit generics or pretyped options. `complete` distinguishes the potentially partial initial snapshot from final output. The removed `getOutputObjectFromRootValue` option rejects. Use named root `rewriteObjectAs<Out>(input, options?)`, namespace `objectRewrite.rewriteObjectAs`, or the rewrite subpath helper for an explicit caller assertion; it performs no schema validation, and property values in its options remain unknown.
1696	
1697	`outputResultAtReturn` captures `ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out>` when the helper returns, possibly partial while halted; it does not refresh on resume. Its variants are `{ kind: 'present', value: Out }` and `{ kind: 'absent' }`. A retained `null` or `undefined` root is present. Absent roots do not invoke `convertRootValue`. Resume through `result.traversalRunner.run()`, then call `result.getOutputResult()` for the final tagged result. The getter requires FINISHED and caches its first successful final conversion/result, reusing the initial result if the first run already finished. Exact conversion errors propagate without caching a success. Result wrappers are frozen; caller values remain shallow. The former scalar `outputAtReturn`/`getOutput()` APIs are removed.
1698	
1699	The helper owns its source. `traversableTree` is forbidden in inline and pretyped options; JavaScript presence, including present `undefined`, rejects before source, rewrite or conversion callbacks. Remove that field, or use a traversal directly for a custom source.
1700	
1701	`createObjectMutationBinder(options)` returns an `ObjectMutationBinder`; binding a vertex and context returns `ObjectMutationCommands`. Its `makeMutationCommand` builder consumes an `ObjectMutationRequest<Output>`. `ObjectMutationOptions` retains classifiers, assemblers, and `assembledMap`, keyed by reference identity. `ObjectCompositeClassification` names the bound array/object/composite flags. Generic stages are `TreeMutationCommandBinderFactory`, `TreeMutationCommandBinder`, `MutationCommands`, `MutationCommandBuilder`, `MutationRequest`, and `MutationCommand`.
1702	
1703	Generic `MutationCommandBuilder<Output, RewriteInput = Output['VertexData']>` uses `{ kind: 'rewrite', value }` for complete replacement data, `{ kind: 'delete' }` for deletion, and `{ kind: 'keep' }` for no mutation. Object helpers explicitly accept `ObjectPropertyPatch<Output>` (`Partial<Pick<Output['VertexData'], 'key' | 'value'>>`), so key-only and value-only patches remain typed. Omit the operation or return `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Object rewrites use `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch }`; the patch must be a non-null object. Malformed or conflicting operations throw TypeError before assembly or mutation. `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { value: undefined } }` sets an undefined value when the output type permits it. User assembler errors propagate exactly. Unknown own patch fields, including non-enumerable string or symbol keys, throw TypeError. Existing payload metadata is retained; use `REWRITE_VERTEX_DATA` for full payload replacement.
1704	
1705	`ObjectRewriteCallback<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>` receives `ObjectRewriteInput` and `ObjectRewriteContext` with the same type parameters. Current keys and `getKeyPath()` include input and output keys. Current values are `unknown`: unchanged values and reconstructed containers can mix retained and replaced children, such as `[1, 'two']`. This applies to callback properties, vertex/ref/live tree, previous refs, classifiers, and assembler parent/child properties. `ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<InputTypes, OutputTypes>` preserves key identity and metadata alternatives without promising a narrow current value domain; narrowing by key or metadata cannot restore one. Assembler results, `assembledComposite`, and assembly cache values are also `unknown`. Requested replacement patches retain their declared `OutV` payload type. `originalTreeView` retains input types. `ObjectTreeVertexTypes<K, V>` names the object vertex-data/hint family; `ResolvedTreeVertexTypes<T>` names a tree whose data/hints are resolved vertex refs.
1706	
1707	Default `ObjectTreeSource` discovery exposes `PropertyKey`/`unknown`. Narrow key or value domains require both `getRootPropertyFromInputObject` and `getChildrenOfProperty`, including through `rewriteObject` options. `ObjectTreeSource.fromProperties(input, { getRootPropertyFromInputObject, getChildrenOfProperty })` provides a precise route with both adapters required and checked before input callbacks. Explicit constructor generics cannot bypass these requirements.
1708	
1709	`assembledMap` accepts `ObjectAssemblyCache<Key>`, a structural protocol with function-valued `has`, `get`, and `set` members. Its writer must accept `unknown`; a `Map<Key, unknown>` works, while `Map<Key, string>` rejects because mixed assembly would invalidate its reads. Cache keys retain reference identity.
1710	
1711	Discovery hints belong to the source input domain: `REWRITE_CHILD_HINTS` accepts `T['VertexHint'][]` in tree and DAG visitors, including async visitors, registration groups and `rewriteObject` options. Rewriting vertex data to `R` does not admit `R['VertexHint']`. `resolveChild`, object `resolveChildHook` and `getChildrenOfProperty` still resolve input records; retained original views therefore remain truthful. If discovery needs another hint kind, declare it in the source input union first. For object sources that means extending `InK`/`InV`, and original views then reflect that declared union.
1712	
1713	A composed source must accept the traversal's full current context. Source callback properties are checked contravariantly with strict function checking: an input-only `ObjectTreeSource<In, InK, InV>` can be too narrow for a traversal that widens live keys or hints. Configure its `OutK`/`OutV` to match, and use `ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<Input, Output>` for the traversal and binder's live data. For custom sources, explicitly declare `TreeSource<T, R>` / `DagDiscoverySource<T, R, ID>` (or their async counterparts) when standalone callbacks do not provide enough inference. Matching sources and binders compose without assertions. On TypeScript 4.7/4.9, put an unannotated hint transformer directly on the options object; for a transformer nested in a spread, use a generic hint-preserving function (`<Hint,>(hints: Hint[]) => hints.reverse()`) or annotate `T['VertexHint'][]`. See the [executable alternatives](migration-idiomatic-api.md#corrected-object-contracts).
1714	
1715	The shared algebra keeps its standalone default while accepting a trailing `SourceHint`: `TraversalVisitorCommandArguments<R, SourceHint = R['VertexHint']>`, `TraversalVisitorCommand<R, Name, SourceHint = R['VertexHint']>`, `TraversalVisitorResult<R, Phase, Family, SourceHint = R['VertexHint']>`. Concrete tree/DAG visitors select `T['VertexHint']` automatically. Existing generic positions, including trailing graph IDs, remain unchanged.
1716	
1717	`ObjectTreeSource.createRootPropertyMapper(rootKey?)` preserves the actual input value type and chosen root-key type; omitting the key exposes the literal default root key. It cannot assert a different value type through generic arguments. `getChildrenOfPropertyDefault` returns `PropertyKey`/`unknown` children for arbitrary properties.
1718	
1719	The binder returns `ObjectMutationCommands<OutputTypes, InputTypes>`: its builder accepts output key/value patches and emits commands containing current records. `rewriteObject` configures this current domain automatically for its visitors, source callback contexts and returned runner. For direct generic traversal composition, use `ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<InputTypes, OutputTypes>` as the traversal's second type argument and as the vertex type of reference-keyed assembly maps. Original retained views still use the first, input type argument.
1720	
1721	<!-- standalone -->
1722	
1723	```ts
1724	import {
1725	  ObjectTreeSource,
1726	  createObjectMutationBinder,
1727	  traverseTreeDepthFirst,
1728	  DepthFirstPhase,
1729	  type ObjectTreeVertexTypes,
1730	  type ObjectCurrentVertexTypes,
1731	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
1732	
1733	type Input = ObjectTreeVertexTypes<'input', number>;
1734	type Output = ObjectTreeVertexTypes<'output', string>;
1735	type Current = ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<Input, Output>;
1736	const bind = createObjectMutationBinder<Input, Output>();
1737	const runner = traverseTreeDepthFirst<Input, Current>({
1738	  traversableTree: new ObjectTreeSource<
1739	    number,
1740	    'input',
1741	    number,
1742	    'output',
1743	    string
1744	  >(1, {
1745	    getRootPropertyFromInputObject: (value) => ({ key: 'input', value }),
1746	    getChildrenOfProperty: () => [],
1747	  }),
1748	  visitors: {
1749	    [DepthFirstPhase.PRE_ORDER]: (vertex, context) => ({
1750	      commands: [
1751	        bind(vertex, context).makeMutationCommand({
1752	          kind: 'rewrite',
1753	          patch: { key: 'output' },
1754	        }),
1755	      ],
1756	    }),
1757	  },
1758	});
1759	const current = runner.getResolvedTreeView().getRoot()!.getValue().getData();
1760	if (current.key !== 'output' || current.value !== 1)
1761	  throw new Error('Expected a key-only patch');
1762	```
1763	
1764	`resolveChildHook(hint, context)` returns `ObjectChildHookResult<T>`: `{ kind: 'useDefault' }`, tagged tree `found` with replacement content, or `{ kind: 'omitted' }`. It applies only to child/hint resolution; use `getRootPropertyFromInputObject` for the root. Null/undefined returns and graph metadata reject. `resolveVertexHook` and `makeVertexHook` reject as unsupported own keys, including undefined/null; `returnMe` hook results reject. Cycle checks and shallow identities remain.
1765	
1766	With `retainOriginalTreeStructure: true`, visitors and child-resolution callbacks receive `originalTreeView: ResolvedTreeView<T> | null`, a stable read-only query facade over the retained original structure. Its vertex references, child lists, and resolution contexts are independent of command-driven changes. Vertex data is shallowly shared, so direct mutation of user data is not an immutable snapshot. The retained tree grows as vertices are resolved. DAG retention uses `retainOriginalGraphStructure`, `originalGraphView`, and `OriginalGraphView` with the same progressive topology and shared-data semantics. Runner configuration and visitor records are also copied when a runner is made; later builder configuration does not alter that runner.

1768	## API compatibility
1769	
1770	The [idiomatic API migration](migration-idiomatic-api.md) covers the full removal checklist and corrected object contracts. The [API naming migration](migration-api-clarity.md) lists renamed symbols, removed public extension points and supported paths. The [uniform API migration guide](migration-uniform-api.md) covers removed inputs and behavior changes. `Vertex` owns enumerable `$data`/`$childHints`; legacy `$d`/`$c` inputs/accessors are removed. Object spread, `Object.keys`, and JSON output use canonical names. `clone({ $data: undefined })` explicitly replaces data. Mixed canonical/legacy content fields reject. Built-in object and resolved-tree source adapters emit canonical content; resolved-tree structural child references remain structural refs.
1771	
1772	CTT 0.11.0 uses UUID 14 and requires Node 22.12.0+ for synchronous ESM dependency loading, or Bun 1.4.4. Public CJS/ESM entry points and TypeScript 4.7.4/4.9.5 consumer compatibility remain covered by packed checks.
1773	
1774	Namespace exports `core`, `depthFirstTraversal`, `breadthFirstTraversal`, `dagTraversal`, `traversableObjectTree`, `objectRewrite`, and `graphWalk` remain available, alongside named exports for all eight traversal builders, helpers, and types. Public subpaths include `core` and each traversal family. Historical deep imports such as `configurable-tree-traversal/core/Vertex` and `configurable-tree-traversal/traversals/dag-traversal/lib/DagTraversalRunner` are blocked, with or without `.js`. Import `Vertex` from root/core and obtain runners through `createRunner()`. See the [complete supported path map](migration-api-clarity.md#supported-imports-and-removed-extension-points).
1775	
1776	Corrected behavior includes independent iteration, reliable halt/resume, terminal error handling, sorting, subtree deletion, and zero-based visitor indices. Root deletion returns a tagged absent result; retaining or rewriting the root to null returns a present result whose value is null. See [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) for the full list.

1792	The tests cover deterministic generated trees and DAGs, mutations, dependencies, async races, pause/resume, failures, snapshots, original-tree isolation, object reconstruction, deep chains, and wide trees. `npm run check` requires 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines across all source files and executes every example. See [the testing guide](testing.md) for the test layout and regression workflow.
1793	
1794	The packed consumer check runs CommonJS, native ESM, and strict TypeScript imports from a temporary extracted tarball, using installed runtime dependencies. It checks classic Node and Node16 TypeScript resolution, mixed `.mts`/`.cts` consumers, all supported entry points and actual denial of private paths, native ESM resolution, and cross-loader identity and DAG lifecycle behavior. It uses `tar` and runs in CI on Linux. Node 22 and 24 run the full check; a separate Bun 1.4.4 lane runs the packed consumers and facade/benchmark correctness tests after an npm build. Jest and source coverage remain Node checks. No package is published by the verification commands. The benchmark compares deep and wide trees with both traversal strategies; timings depend on the machine and are not performance guarantees.
1795	
1796	The DAG inspector benchmark emits JSON with the loaded artifact/version, machine details, raw samples, and warmup-excluded medians/ranges. It covers five dependency shapes with empty and prerequisite-closed prefix seeds, full eager discovery, deferral admission, and repeated summaries. For registry-package reproduction, exact timing boundaries, and the limited independent Kahn baseline, see [the DAG baseline](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/docs/performance/2026-10-22-dag-baseline.md). Run `npm run build && npm run test:benchmark` for focused fixture, frontier, purity, and CLI checks.
1797	
1798	The lifecycle benchmark measures sync/async and eager/lazy runners separately, including bounded settlement batches, resumed runs, reconstruction from the same accepted completion facts, and summaries. Its async visitor awaits a resolved Promise, measuring callback scheduling overhead. JSON records exact settlement counts, partial lazy discovery, artifact tree hashes, raw ticks, and timing boundaries. Counts are bounded positive integers; `--library-path` selects a package directory or entry. See [the lifecycle measurements](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/docs/performance/2026-10-22-dag-lifecycle.md) for results and limitations. Both benchmark correctness suites run after the build in `npm run check`.
1799	
1800	Retries, durable checkpoints, and callback cancellation are outside this release. User vertex data is not frozen. Discovery cycles are rejected; dependency cycles or missing dependencies fail as a scheduling stall.

[Documentation map](index.md) · [Behavior reference](reference.md) · [Upgrade checklist](migration-api-distinctions.md)

These declarations describe the [unreleased source checkout](../README.md#install). Look up a current exported name below, then follow its owning contract and runnable example. Public import routes are exhaustive for each symbol; declaration-module paths are not consumer imports.

Generated from the supported declaration census: **271 public symbols**, **540 export bindings**, **9 runtime entry points**. Run `npm run docs:api` to regenerate; package verification rejects stale output.

Declaration excerpts preserve overloads and public members; referenced support types can be declaration-local and are not additional importable exports. Inline declaration-relative type imports are displayed by type name. These are declaration excerpts, not standalone programs; the linked guide examples are compiled and executed against the packed package. docs/migration-api-clarity.md:94:`defineDag` copies/normalizes authored declarations; `prepareDagDefinition` validates/prepares them. `prepareDag`, `composeDag`, `reviseDag` and `diffDagDefinitions` keep their distinct effects. Definitions preserve ordered omitted slots; the prepared `.liveVertexSummaries` projection includes only live structural children. Session `advance`, `failTraversal`, registration methods, `run`, `configure` and graph-walking strategy/revisit configuration remain receiver-scoped operations.
docs/migration-uniform-api.md:33:These optional APIs extend prepared DAGs. `prepared.definition` retains entry mode, ordered discovery slots and omissions; `.liveVertexSummaries` is a live-child convenience projection and rebuilding from it loses those facts. Use `definition.vertices` when authoring revisions. Author values with `defineDag`, validate with `prepareDagDefinition`, or reuse shapes through `defineDagFragment`, `mapDagFragmentIds` and `composeDag`. 1	# Working on configurable-tree-traversal
2	
3	## Read the right entry point
4	
5	- **Using CTT in an agent coordinator:** start at [README](README.md), then [agent workflows](docs/agent-workflows.md).
6	- **Finding a public contract:** [API reference](docs/reference.md), or [symbol index](docs/api-index.md) for exact exported names/signatures. [Documentation map](docs/index.md) links runnable examples.
7	- **Changing this repository:** use the source/test map below and [testing guide](docs/testing.md).
8	
9	The [API distinctions migration](docs/migration-api-distinctions.md) covers the latest twenty findings and canonical surface. The [client API migration](docs/migration-client-api.md) covers the twenty client contract corrections. The [idiomatic API migration](docs/migration-idiomatic-api.md) covers the canonical removal checklist and corrected object contracts. The [migration guide](docs/migration-uniform-api.md) covers changed defaults and removed compatibility forms. `docs/research/` and `docs/superpowers/` contain historical research, plans, and downstream proposals. They are not a substitute for current documentation or evidence that a proposed feature exists. Reconcile discrepancies against source and behavioral tests; update the current guide when changing behavior.
10	
11	## Scope and boundaries
12	
13	CTT owns generic tree/graph discovery, work/completion dependencies, callback scheduling, traversal lifecycle, diagnostics, and in-memory progress. Keep task types, agent dispatch, business priority/outcomes, attempts/retries, claims, artifact policy, and durable storage in the host. `$data` is opaque caller data; `$childHints` contains opaque discovery hints. `$d`/`$c` inputs and accessors are removed; Vertex fields and serialization use `$data`/`$childHints`. There is no public `planDag`, storage-provider port, durable runner checkpoint, or built-in LLM integration.
14	
15	Dependency edges and structural child edges are different. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal `ON_WORK_READY` completion satisfies W; committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` satisfies C. Use `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` for host-controlled work, including zero/filtered callbacks; prepare a fresh runner for an eager validated preview, then run and dispatch from `summary().awaitingSettlement` records with atomic generation guards. Preparation freezes topology; run adopts discovery without replay. Dispatch from `advance().workTickets` or enabled pre-work visitors. DAG event kinds `workCompleted`/`subgraphCompleted` are committed W/C observations; callback-before-commit and event-after-commit timing remain. Deferred `workCompleted` events emit on settlement; seeds synthesize no work event. Explicit sole `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` ends a chain early; `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` pauses it. `getStopReason()` distinguishes pause from awaiting settlement. Graph sources default to `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`; express execution dependencies explicitly. Explicit graph dependency policies reject on TreeSource inputs; tree order is preserved. Deletion commands follow the runner family: `DELETE_TREE_SUBTREE` or `DELETE_DAG_VERTEX_CASCADE`. Stored-tree deletion is `deleteSubtree`, revision removal is `removeVertexDeclaration`, and multi-entry definitions use ordered `roots` slots. `SKIP_REMAINING_CHILDREN` skips pending local expansion; `SET_VISITOR_CHAIN_STATE` accepts `{ state }` for the current phase chain. Source callbacks use tagged `found`/`omitted` results; only prerequisite lookup accepts `missing`. `emitEvents` and `visitorPhases` select events/callbacks independently and patch field-wise. Flat visitors sort by priority before batching; explicit ordered groups own their batching policy. `commandCommitMode` is independent of async concurrency. Tree sources forbid graph metadata. Prefer `resolveChildHook`, typed object patches, `getResolvedTreeView()`, `getRefId()` and graph `requireVertexId`/`getVertexRefById`; ordinary tree/DAG observations expose canonical VertexHandle/VertexView facets, frozen detached hint/topology collections, and shallow caller payload identity. Tree contexts use resolvedTreeView; graph contexts use resolvedGraphView/getResolvedGraphView. Ordinary runners expose no live mutable store or independent traversal-root predicate. Synthetic entry source parents have both parent fields null; tree parents stay non-null. Use family-safe execution capabilities and cooperative `requestPause`; requests drain admitted callbacks without cancellation before acknowledgement. Rewrite output uses present/absent tagged results and defaults to unknown; `rewriteObjectAs` asserts output and `getOutputResult()` requires FINISHED. The rewrite helper owns its source. Visitor registration queries return detached records with shared callbacks/group metadata. Graph ID generics trail T/R (visitor ID follows phase); typed live results require own IDs and public views hide synthetic holders. Runner constructors, raw containers/state, normalized options and deep engine paths are private; use public factories, capability interfaces and the explicit supported entry points. Diagnostic edges are original milestone constraints, waiter waits for prerequisite; structural cycle componentVertexIds are SCC membership; discovery cycleWitnessVertexIds are ordered closed witnesses. Settlement generations are local symbols; reconstruction uses host-accepted `completedWork` facts. `inspectDagMilestones` captures observational milestone snapshots. Inspection uses ready/chain `phase`, chain `state`/`visitorIndex`/`executionOptions`, and request `operation`; graph `visitStage`/`getVisitStageOf` describes scheduling boundaries, separately from callback counts, DAG W/C, and runner lifecycle status. `PreparedDag.liveVertexSummaries` is a live-child convenience projection; `PreparedDag.definition` preserves ordered slots/omissions; mapDagFragmentIds maps fragment IDs explicitly and compose structural links separately from W/C wires. `reviseDag` validates an ordered batch against a private candidate and returns a fresh prepared DAG plus a shallow diff; old sessions, tickets and admitted callbacks remain local and no completion facts migrate.
16	
17	`MaterializedDagInput` and `materializeDagInputFromRecords`/`materializeDagInputFromRoots` (plus Async counterparts) return `{ traversableGraph, syntheticRoot: true }` envelopes. Pass or spread the entire input; `DagDiscoverySource` is the actual protocol. Walking materializers return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols and retain source names.
18	
19	Walking uses `GraphWalk`/`AsyncGraphWalk` sources with explicit target wrappers; it does not consume arbitrary tree/DAG sources directly. Revisit, callbacks and emission are independent. First admitted resolution (including omission) wins; rejected links do not seed cache. Default once preserves parallel/back edges; bounded route modes report summary outcomes. All family selectors filter at delivery, including buffered records and deferred settlement events; callback admission snapshots stay independent. Chain inspection emitEvents is historical, while top-level executionOptions governs delivery. Callbacks are serial; own concurrency options reject. Consumer iterator return pauses; terminal runner close disposes open source iterators in reverse acquisition order. Closing FAILED rethrows the exact retained error without repeated cleanup; overlapping async closes share a promise. Configure replaceLimits records replace prior limits records and merged validation is atomic. `GraphWalkDagRelation` labels are adapter-owned/detached; caller edge data retains identity. General execution capabilities default to `ExecutionInspection` and `EmissionKind<Phase>`, preserving family phases. Concrete tree/DAG runners use `TreeDagExecutionInspection`; walkers use `GraphWalkInspection`. Tree callbacks use `TreeVisitor`/`AsyncTreeVisitor`, with structural source protocols and no empty runtime bases.
20	
21	## Source and regression map
22	
23	| Change area                             | Start in                                                                                                                                          | Relevant tests                                                                                                                                |
24	| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
25	| General graph walking                   | `src/traversals/graph-walk/`, `lib/WalkKernel.ts`, sync/async sessions and resources                                                              | `tests/graph-walk-*.test.ts`, walking type assertions, packed `graph-walk` consumers                                                          |
26	| Public exports and graph types          | `src/index.ts`, `src/core/TraversableGraph.ts`, `src/core/TraversableTree.ts`                                                                     | `tests/public-api.typecheck.ts`, `tests/graph-api.typecheck.ts`, `scripts/verify-package.cjs`                                                 |
27	| DAG dependency queries and explanations | `src/traversals/dag-traversal/inspectDag.ts`, `src/core/TraversalKernel.ts`                                                                       | `tests/dag-inspection.test.ts`, `tests/dag-inspection.typecheck.ts`                                                                           |
28	| DAG definitions and fragments           | `src/traversals/dag-traversal/defineDag.ts`, `prepareDagDefinition.ts`, `dagFragments.ts`, `src/traversals/dag-traversal/lib/definitionSource.ts` | `tests/dag-definition.test.ts`, `tests/dag-definition-validation.test.ts`, `tests/dag-fragments.test.ts`, definition/fragment type assertions |
29	| DAG revisions and declaration diffs     | `src/traversals/dag-traversal/reviseDag.ts`, `diffDagDefinitions.ts`, `lib/DagRevision.ts`                                                        | `tests/dag-revisions.test.ts`, `tests/dag-revisions.typecheck.ts`, packed `dag-revisions` consumers                                           |
30	| DAG readiness, progress and milestones  | `src/core/scheduling/GraphScheduling.ts`, `src/core/scheduling/dependencyMilestones.ts`                                                           | `tests/dag-progress-seed.test.ts`, `tests/dag-completion-dependencies.test.ts`, `tests/graph-completion-dependencies.test.ts`                 |
31	| Prerequisite lookup and lifecycle       | `src/core/scheduling/PrerequisiteResolution.ts`, `src/core/TraversalKernel.ts`                                                                    | `tests/dag-prerequisite-resolution.test.ts`, `tests/async-dag-prerequisite-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/prerequisite-kernel.test.ts`            |
